udyogasamayastveṣa prāptaḥ śatruvināśana
saṁcintyatāṁ hi piṅgeśa haribhiḥ saha mantribhiḥ
O destroyer of foes, the time is come for exertion: do you, O lord of monkeys, bethink yourself along with your monkey ministers.

प्रनष्टा श्रीश्च कीर्तिश्च कपिराज्यं च शाश्वतम्
त्वत्प्रसादान्महाबाहो पुनः प्राप्तमिदं मया

pranaṣṭā śrīśca kīrtiśca kapirājyaṁ ca śāśvatam
tvatprasādānmahābāho punaḥ prāptamidaṁ mayā

Thus addressed, Sugriva said to Rama, O mighty-armed one, my lost luck, and repute, and the entire monkey kingdom I have received back through your gift, owing to thine and your brother's grace, you foremost of victors.

तव देवप्रसदाच्च भ्रातुश्च जयतां वर
कृतं न प्रतिकुर्याद्यः पुरुषाणां स दूषकः

tava devaprasadācca bhrātuśca jayatāṁ vara
kṛtaṁ na pratikuryādyaḥ puruṣāṇāṁ sa dūṣakaḥ
He that, having received a good office, does not requite it, reapeth obloquy among persons.

एते वानरमुख्याश्च शतशः शत्रुसूदन
प्राप्ताश्चादाय बलिनः पृथिव्यां सर्ववानरान्

ete vānaramukhyāśca śataśaḥ śatrusūdana
prāptāścādāya balinaḥ pṛthivyāṁ sarvavānarān
These hundreds of prime monkeys, O destroyer of enemies, have come here, bringing with them all the monkeys of the world.

ते त्वामभिगमिष्यन्ति राक्षसं ये सबान्धवम्
निहत्य रावणं संख्ये ह्यानयिष्यन्ति मैथिलीम्

te tvāmabhigamiṣyanti rākṣasaṁ ye sabāndhavam
nihatya rāvaṇaṁ saṁkhye hyānayiṣyanti maithilīm
They will join you for battling the fiend in the field; and, slaying Ravana in fight, shall bring Mithila's daughter.

ततस्तमुद्योगमवेक्ष्य बुद्धिमा;न्हरिप्रवीरस्य निदेशवर्तिनः
बभूव हर्षाद्वसुधाधिपात्मजः; प्रबुद्धनीलोत्पलतुल्यदर्शनः

tatastamudyogamavekṣya buddhimā;nharipravīrasya nideśavartinaḥ
babhūva harṣādvasudhādhipātmajaḥ; prabuddhanīlotpalatulyadarśanaḥ
Thereat the puissant son of the Earth's lord, witnessing the preparations made by the heroic monkey, remaining under his his command, appeared like a blown blue lotus.

इति ब्रुवाणं सुग्रीवं रामो धर्मभृतां वरः
बाहुभ्यां संपरिष्वज्य प्रत्युवाच कृताञ्जलिम्

iti bruvāṇaṁ sugrīvaṁ rāmo dharmabhṛtāṁ varaḥ
bāhubhyāṁ saṁpariṣvajya pratyuvāca kṛtāñjalim
As Sugriva was speaking thus with joined hands, that best of the righteous, Rama, embraced him with his arms, and then replied,

यदिन्द्रो वर्षते वर्षं न तच्चित्रं भवेद्भुवि
आदित्यो वा सहस्रांशुः कुर्याद्वितिमिरं नभः

yadindro varṣate varṣaṁ na taccitraṁ bhavedbhuvi
ādityo vā sahasrāṁśuḥ kuryādvitimiraṁ nabhaḥ

That Indra poureth down showers, is no wonder, nor that this thousand-rayed Sun dispels darkness from the sky; nor yet that, O mild one, the Moon by his rays causes the clear night. (And in a similar way), friends like you bring delight, O subduer of foes. O mild one, that 'whatever is graceful, should be harboured in you is not strange.* *The commentator in his usual way of reading between the lines, says that the sense is—That you had gathered forces for serving your friend, is not strange. O placid one, it is well. I give the sense the sloka naturally yields.

एवं त्वयि न तच्चित्रं भवेद्यत्सौम्य शोभनम्
जानाम्यहं त्वां सुग्रीव सततं प्रियवादिनम्

evaṁ tvayi na taccitraṁ bhavedyatsaumya śobhanam
jānāmyahaṁ tvāṁ sugrīva satataṁ priyavādinam
I know, O Sugriva, that you always speakst what is for my good.

त्वत्सनाथः सखे संख्ये जेतास्मि सकलानरीन्
त्वमेव मे सुहृन्मित्रं साहाय्यं कर्तुमर्हसि

tvatsanāthaḥ sakhe saṁkhye jetāsmi sakalānarīn
tvameva me suhṛnmitraṁ sāhāyyaṁ kartumarhasi
Assisted by you, my friend, I shall in battle vanquish all my foes. You being my friend and my ally, should assist me.

जहारात्मविनाशाय वैदेहीं राक्षसाधमः
वञ्चयित्वा तु पौलोमीमनुह्लादो यथा शचीम्

jahārātmavināśāya vaidehīṁ rākṣasādhamaḥ
vañcayitvā tu paulomīmanuhlādo yathā śacīm
That worst of Raksasas has carried away Maithili, to bring down destruction upon himself, even as Anuhlada ravished Puloma's daughter, Sachi, deceiving her sire.

नचिरात्तं हनिष्यामि रावणं निशितैः शरैः
पौलोम्याः पितरं दृप्तं शतक्रतुरिवारिहा

nacirāttaṁ haniṣyāmi rāvaṇaṁ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
paulomyāḥ pitaraṁ dṛptaṁ śatakraturivārihā
That Ravana I will at no distant date slay with my sharpened shafts, even as that slayer of enemies, he of an hundred sacrifices-slew the haughty father of Paulomi.

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे चैव रजः समभिवर्तत
उष्णां तीव्रां सहस्रांशोश्छादयद्गगने प्रभाम्

etasminnantare caiva rajaḥ samabhivartata
uṣṇāṁ tīvrāṁ sahasrāṁśośchādayadgagane prabhām
Presently appeared volumes of dust, and the hot and fierce rays of the sun were hid in the sky.

दिशः पर्याकुलाश्चासन्रजसा तेन मूर्छिताः
चचाल च मही सर्वा सशैलवनकानना

diśaḥ paryākulāścāsanrajasā tena mūrchitāḥ
cacāla ca mahī sarvā saśailavanakānanā
And darkened by the gloom, all sides became bewildered. And the entire earth with her mountains, forests, and wocds, trembled.

ततो नगेन्द्रसंकाशैस्तीक्ष्ण दंष्ट्रैर्महाबलैः
कृत्स्ना संछादिता भूमिरसंख्येयैः प्लवंगमैः

tato nagendrasaṁkāśaistīkṣṇa daṁṣṭrairmahābalaiḥ
kṛtsnā saṁchāditā bhūmirasaṁkhyeyaiḥ plavaṁgamaiḥ
Then the whole ground was covered with innumerable monkeys gifted with great strength, and having sharp teeth, and resembling kings of men.

ततः काञ्चनशैलाभस्ताराया वीर्यवान्पिता
अनेकैर्दशसाहस्रैः कोटिभिः प्रत्यदृश्यत

tataḥ kāñcanaśailābhastārāyā vīryavānpitā
anekairdaśasāhasraiḥ koṭibhiḥ pratyadṛśyata
Then, having the splendour of the Golden hill, the puissant sire of Tara was seen at the head of many thousand kotis.

अनीकैर्बहुसाहस्रैर्वानराणां समन्वितः
पिता हनुमतः श्रीमान्केसरी प्रत्यदृश्यत

anīkairbahusāhasrairvānarāṇāṁ samanvitaḥ
pitā hanumataḥ śrīmānkesarī pratyadṛśyata
And Hanuman's father, the graceful Kasari, appeared in company with many thousands of monkeys.

गोलाङ्गूलमहाराजो गवाक्षो भीमविक्रमः
वृतः कोटिसहस्रेण वानराणामदृश्यत

golāṅgūlamahārājo gavākṣo bhīmavikramaḥ
vṛtaḥ koṭisahasreṇa vānarāṇāmadṛśyata
And Gavaksa-sovereign of Golangulas-endowed with dreadful might, appeared, surrounded by thousand kotis of monkeys.

ऋक्षाणां भीमवेगानां धूम्रः शत्रुनिबर्हणः
वृतः कोटिसहस्राभ्यां द्वाभ्यां समभिवर्तत

ṛkṣāṇāṁ bhīmavegānāṁ dhūmraḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ
vṛtaḥ koṭisahasrābhyāṁ dvābhyāṁ samabhivartata
And Dhumra of bears endowed with terrific speed—destroyer of foes—appeared, surrounded by two thousand kotis.

महाचलनिभैर्घोरैः पनसो नाम यूथपः
आजगाम महावीर्यस्तिसृभिः कोटिभिर्वृतः

mahācalanibhairghoraiḥ panaso nāma yūthapaḥ
ājagāma mahāvīryastisṛbhiḥ koṭibhirvṛtaḥ
And the leader of herds, named Panasa, of exceeding prowess, came, accompanied with three kotis, mighty and dreadful.

नीलाञ्जनचयाकारो नीलो नामाथ यूथपः
अदृश्यत महाकायः कोटिभिर्दशभिर्वृतः

nīlāñjanacayākāro nīlo nāmātha yūthapaḥ
adṛśyata mahākāyaḥ koṭibhirdaśabhirvṛtaḥ
And the leader of herds, named Nila, of huge body, resembling a mass of blue collyrium. appeared with ten kotis.

दरीमुखश्च बलवान्यूथपोऽभ्याययौ तदा
वृतः कोटिसहस्रेण सुग्रीवं समुपस्थितः

darīmukhaśca balavānyūthapo'bhyāyayau tadā
vṛtaḥ koṭisahasreṇa sugrīvaṁ samupasthitaḥ
And that powerful leader of herdsDarimukha, came, sutrounded by thousands of kotis, and took up his post by Sugriva.

मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चोभावश्विपुत्रौ महावलौ
कोटिकोटिसहस्रेण वानराणामदृश्यताम्

maindaśca dvividaścobhāvaśviputrau mahāvalau
koṭikoṭisahasreṇa vānarāṇāmadṛśyatām
And Mainda and Dvivida-sons of Asvi both-of mighty strength, appeared with kotis upon thousands of kotis of monkeys.

ततः कोटिसहस्राणां सहस्रेण शतेन च
पृष्ठतोऽनुगतः प्राप्तो हरिभिर्गन्धमादनः

tataḥ koṭisahasrāṇāṁ sahasreṇa śatena ca
pṛṣṭhato'nugataḥ prāpto haribhirgandhamādanaḥ
Then, followed at his back by hundreds and thousands of kotis, came the monkey, Gandhamadana.

ततः पद्मसहस्रेण वृतः शङ्कुशतेन च
युवराजोऽङ्गदः प्राप्तः पितृतुल्यपराक्रमः

tataḥ padmasahasreṇa vṛtaḥ śaṅkuśatena ca
yuvarājo'ṅgadaḥ prāptaḥ pitṛtulyaparākramaḥ
Then came the young prince Angada, in prowess resembling his sire, accompanied by a thousand padmas and an hundred sankhas.

ततस्ताराद्युतिस्तारो हरिर्भीमपराक्रमः
पञ्चभिर्हरिकोटीभिर्दूरतः प्रत्यदृश्यत

tatastārādyutistāro harirbhīmaparākramaḥ
pañcabhirharikoṭībhirdūrataḥ pratyadṛśyata
Then appeared at a distance, accompanied by five kotis of monkeys endowed with dreadful prowess,-Tara, having the splendour of a star.

इन्द्रजानुः कपिर्वीरो यूथपः प्रत्यदृश्यत
एकादशानां कोटीनामीश्वरस्तैश्च संवृतः

indrajānuḥ kapirvīro yūthapaḥ pratyadṛśyata
ekādaśānāṁ koṭīnāmīśvarastaiśca saṁvṛtaḥ
And then appeared Indrajani, the heroic monkey and leader of herds-lord of eleven kotis-surrounded by them.

ततो रम्भस्त्वनुप्राप्तस्तरुणादित्यसंनिभः
अयुतेन वृतश्चैव सहस्रेण शतेन च

tato rambhastvanuprāptastaruṇādityasaṁnibhaḥ
ayutena vṛtaścaiva sahasreṇa śatena ca
Then followed Rambha, resembling the infant sun, accompanied by an ayuta, a thousand, and an hundred.

ततो यूथपतिर्वीरो दुर्मुखो नाम वानरः
प्रत्यदृश्यत कोटिभ्यां द्वाभ्यां परिवृतो बली

tato yūthapatirvīro durmukho nāma vānaraḥ
pratyadṛśyata koṭibhyāṁ dvābhyāṁ parivṛto balī
Then appeared to the view the stout monkey, named Durmukha, heroic lord of herds, surrounded by two kotis.

कैलासशिखराकारैर्वानरैर्भीमविक्रमैः
वृतः कोटिसहस्रेण हनुमान्प्रत्यदृश्यत

kailāsaśikharākārairvānarairbhīmavikramaiḥ
vṛtaḥ koṭisahasreṇa hanumānpratyadṛśyata
And Hanuman showed himself, surrounded by a thousand kotis of monkeys, resembling peaks of Kailasa, of dreadful vigour.

नलश्चापि महावीर्यः संवृतो द्रुमवासिभिः
कोटीशतेन संप्राप्तः सहस्रेण शतेन च

nalaścāpi mahāvīryaḥ saṁvṛto drumavāsibhiḥ
koṭīśatena saṁprāptaḥ sahasreṇa śatena ca
And the exceedingly energetic Nala came, attended with an hundred kotis, a thousand, and an hundred monkeys, living in trees.

शरभः कुमुदो वह्निर्वानरो रम्भ एव च
एते चान्ये च बहवो वानराः कामरूपिणः

śarabhaḥ kumudo vahnirvānaro rambha eva ca
ete cānye ca bahavo vānarāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
And Sarabha, Kumuda, Vahni, the monkey Rambha,-and many other monkeys-lords of herds-passing ennumeration-wearing shapes at will, came covering the entire earth with her mountains and forests.

आवृत्य पृथिवीं सर्वां पर्वतांश्च वनानि च
आप्लवन्तः प्लवन्तश्च गर्जन्तश्च प्लवंगमाः
अभ्यवर्तन्त सुग्रीवं सूर्यमभ्रगणा इव

āvṛtya pṛthivīṁ sarvāṁ parvatāṁśca vanāni ca
āplavantaḥ plavantaśca garjantaśca plavaṁgamāḥ
abhyavartanta sugrīvaṁ sūryamabhragaṇā iva

And all the monkeys of the world were some of them coming and others putting up. And monkeys-some of them dripping, and some leaping, and some roaring-gathered round Sugriva, like clouds gathering round the sun.

कुर्वाणा बहुशब्दांश्च प्रहृष्टा बलशालिनः
शिरोभिर्वानरेन्द्राय सुग्रीवाय न्यवेदयन्

kurvāṇā bahuśabdāṁśca prahṛṣṭā balaśālinaḥ
śirobhirvānarendrāya sugrīvāya nyavedayan
And, crying in various tones, prime monkeys furnished with arms, with bent heads spoke humbly to that lord of monkeys—Sugriva.

अपरे वानरश्रेष्ठाः संगम्य च यथोचितम्
सुग्रीवेण समागम्य स्थिताः प्राञ्जलयस्तदा

apare vānaraśreṣṭhāḥ saṁgamya ca yathocitam
sugrīveṇa samāgamya sthitāḥ prāñjalayastadā
And other foremost of monkeys, gathering together duly, came before Sugriva with joined hands.

यथा सुखं पर्वतनिर्झरेषु; वनेषु सर्वेषु च वानरेन्द्राः
निवेशयित्वा विधिवद्बलानि; बलं बलज्ञः प्रतिपत्तुमीष्टे

yathā sukhaṁ parvatanirjhareṣu; vaneṣu sarveṣu ca vānarendrāḥ
niveśayitvā vidhivadbalāni; balaṁ balajñaḥ pratipattumīṣṭe

Sugriva standing with joined hands, expeditiously informed Rama of the arrival of the monkey-leaders in hot haste; and then spoke (to them, saying, O chiefs of monkeys, stationing the forces duly near mountain-rills and all the woods, let him that is conversant with the army, ascertain who have come and who have not.

अथ राजा समृद्धार्थः सुग्रीवः प्लवगेश्वरः
उवाच नरशार्दूलं रामं परबलार्दनम्

atha rājā samṛddhārthaḥ sugrīvaḥ plavageśvaraḥ
uvāca naraśārdūlaṁ rāmaṁ parabalārdanam
Then that lord of monkeys, the successful Sugriva, spoke to Rama-lion among men and destroyer of hostile hosts-saying,

आगता विनिविष्टाश्च बलिनः कामरूपिणः
वानरेन्द्रा महेन्द्राभा ये मद्विषयवासिनः

āgatā viniviṣṭāśca balinaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
vānarendrā mahendrābhā ye madviṣayavāsinaḥ
Those foremost monkeys endued strength and capable of wearing any shape at will, and possessed of the splendour of the mishty Indra,-that inhabit my territories, have come and stationed themselves.

त इमे बहुसाहस्रैर्हरिभिर्भीमविक्रमैः
आगता वानरा घोरा दैत्यदानवसंनिभाः

ta ime bahusāhasrairharibhirbhīmavikramaiḥ
āgatā vānarā ghorā daityadānavasaṁnibhāḥ
And in company with many thousands and innumerable ones that have shewn their ability in many a field, have come monkeys dreadful, and resembling Daityas and Danavas.

ख्यातकर्मापदानाश्च बलवन्तो जितक्लमाः
पराक्रमेषु विख्याता व्यवसायेषु चोत्तमाः

khyātakarmāpadānāśca balavanto jitaklamāḥ
parākrameṣu vikhyātā vyavasāyeṣu cottamāḥ

And these monkeys-dreadful, and resembling Daityas and Danvas are accompanied by powerful monkeys of terrific prowess, who have displayed their virtue in many a field, and are of famed renown in battle and, powerful, and who have mastered languor and are celebrated in prowess and sterling in their profession.

पृथिव्यम्बुचरा राम नानानगनिवासिनः
कोट्यग्रश इमे प्राप्ता वानरास्तव किंकराः

pṛthivyambucarā rāma nānānaganivāsinaḥ
koṭyagraśa ime prāptā vānarāstava kiṁkarāḥ
O Rama, these kotis of apes that have arrived, inhabiting earth and water and various mountainous tracts, are at your service.

निदेशवर्तिनः सर्वे सर्वे गुरुहिते रताः
अभिप्रेतमनुष्ठातुं तव शक्ष्यन्त्यरिंदम

nideśavartinaḥ sarve sarve guruhite ratāḥ
abhipretamanuṣṭhātuṁ tava śakṣyantyariṁdama
All abide by your command all are intent upon the welfare of their master, and, O subduer of foes, they are competent to bring about your end.

यन्मन्यसे नरव्याघ्र प्राप्तकालं तदुच्यताम्
तत्सैन्यं त्वद्वशे युक्तमाज्ञापयितुमर्हसि

yanmanyase naravyāghra prāptakālaṁ taducyatām
tatsainyaṁ tvadvaśe yuktamājñāpayitumarhasi
If, O lion among men, you conceive that the time is ripe, tell it (to me). It behoves you to command those forces, remaining under your sway.

काममेषामिदं कार्यं विदितं मम तत्त्वतः
तथापि तु यथा तत्त्वमाज्ञापयितुमर्हसि

kāmameṣāmidaṁ kāryaṁ viditaṁ mama tattvataḥ
tathāpi tu yathā tattvamājñāpayitumarhasi
Although I am full well acquainted with the work in which they are to be employed, yet you ought to order them as to what they are to accomplish.

तथा ब्रुवाणं सुग्रीवं रामो दशरथात्मजः
बाहुभ्यां संपरिष्वज्य इदं वचनमब्रवीत्

tathā bruvāṇaṁ sugrīvaṁ rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ
bāhubhyāṁ saṁpariṣvajya idaṁ vacanamabravīt
When Sugriva had spoken thus, Dasaratha's son, Rama, embracing him with his arms, said,

ज्ञायतां सौम्य वैदेही यदि जीवति वा न वा
स च देशो महाप्राज्ञ यस्मिन्वसति रावणः

jñāyatāṁ saumya vaidehī yadi jīvati vā na vā
sa ca deśo mahāprājña yasminvasati rāvaṇaḥ
O placid one, do you learn whether Videha's daughter is alive or not; as well as ascertain the country, where, O you endowed with eminent wisdom,.liveth Ravana.

अधिगम्य च वैदेहीं निलयं रावणस्य च
प्राप्तकालं विधास्यामि तस्मिन्काले सह त्वया

adhigamya ca vaidehīṁ nilayaṁ rāvaṇasya ca
prāptakālaṁ vidhāsyāmi tasminkāle saha tvayā
Having come at Vaidehi and Ravana's abode, shall I then appoint the time along with you.

नाहमस्मिन्प्रभुः कार्ये वानरेश न लक्ष्मणः
त्वमस्य हेतुः कार्यस्य प्रभुश्च प्लवगेश्वर

nāhamasminprabhuḥ kārye vānareśa na lakṣmaṇaḥ
tvamasya hetuḥ kāryasya prabhuśca plavageśvara
O lord of monkeys, I am not the master in this matter, nor Laksmana: you are the cause of this undertaking, as well as, O monarch of monkeys, the lord.

त्वमेवाज्ञापय विभो मम कार्यविनिश्चयम्
त्वं हि जानासि यत्कार्यं मम वीर न संशयः

tvamevājñāpaya vibho mama kāryaviniścayam
tvaṁ hi jānāsi yatkāryaṁ mama vīra na saṁśayaḥ
Do you therefore, O lord, command these as to what is to be done by them in my behalf. O hero, you certainly know my business.

सुहृद्द्वितीयो विक्रान्तः प्राज्ञः कालविशेषवित्
भवानस्मद्धिते युक्तः सुकृतार्थोऽर्थवित्तमः

suhṛddvitīyo vikrāntaḥ prājñaḥ kālaviśeṣavit
bhavānasmaddhite yuktaḥ sukṛtārtho'rthavittamaḥ
My second friend (Laksmana being first), you potent, wise, conversant with seasonableness, cognisant of profit, and engaged in our welfare.

एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवो विनतं नाम यूथपम्
अब्रवीद्राम साम्निध्ये लक्ष्मणस्य च धीमतः
शैलाभं मेघनिर्घोषमूर्जितं प्लवगेश्वरम्

evamuktastu sugrīvo vinataṁ nāma yūthapam
abravīdrāma sāmnidhye lakṣmaṇasya ca dhīmataḥ
śailābhaṁ meghanirghoṣamūrjitaṁ plavageśvaram

Thus addressed, Sugriva in presence of Rama and the intelligent Laksmana, said to a leader of herds of lord of apes, named Vinata, having the splendour of a hill, blazing and emitting sounds as those of clouds, O foremost of monkeys, accompanied with apes resembling the sun and the moon, you cognizant of time, place and morals, and sagacious in deciding course of action,-surrounded by hundreds and thousands are of active apes, march towards the Estern quarter, furnished with woods, forests and hills. There, in mountain fastnesses, and forests and rivers, do you search Videha's daughter, Sita, as well as the abode of Ravana.

सुवर्णरूप्यकं चैव सुवर्णाकरमण्डितम्
यवद्वीपमतिक्रम्य शिशिरो नाम पर्वतः

suvarṇarūpyakaṁ caiva suvarṇākaramaṇḍitam
yavadvīpamatikramya śiśiro nāma parvataḥ
And, going beyond the island of Yava. (one comes upon) the hill called Sisira, which pierceth the heavens by its peaks, and is inhabited by gods and demons.

दिवं स्पृशति शृङ्गेण देवदानवसेवितः
एतेषां गिरिदुर्गेषु प्रतापेषु वनेषु च

divaṁ spṛśati śṛṅgeṇa devadānavasevitaḥ
eteṣāṁ giridurgeṣu pratāpeṣu vaneṣu ca
In all these mountain fastnesses, cascades and woods, do you together search for the renowned wife of Rama.

रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः
ततः समुद्रद्वीपांश्च सुभीमान्द्रष्टुमर्हथ

rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyastatastataḥ
tataḥ samudradvīpāṁśca subhīmāndraṣṭumarhatha
Then it behoves you to examine horrible ocean islands, heaving with waves, terrific, resounding,-of haughty bearing in consequence of winds.

तत्रासुरा महाकायाश्छायां गृह्णन्ति नित्यशः
ब्रह्मणा समनुज्ञाता दीर्घकालं बुभुक्षिताः

tatrāsurā mahākāyāśchāyāṁ gṛhṇanti nityaśaḥ
brahmaṇā samanujñātā dīrghakālaṁ bubhukṣitāḥ
There, huge-bodied Asuras, hungering for a long period, permitted by Brahma, capture creatures, resorting to shades.

तं कालमेघप्रतिमं महोरगनिषेवितम्
अभिगम्य महानादं तीर्थेनैव महोदधिम्

taṁ kālameghapratimaṁ mahoraganiṣevitam
abhigamya mahānādaṁ tīrthenaiva mahodadhim
And adroitly arriving at that great sea, like to clouds at the universal dissolution, inhabited by mighty snakes, sending loud sounds.

तत्र शैलनिभा भीमा मन्देहा नाम राक्षसाः
शैलशृङ्गेषु लम्बन्ते नानारूपा भयावहाः

tatra śailanibhā bhīmā mandehā nāma rākṣasāḥ
śailaśṛṅgeṣu lambante nānārūpā bhayāvahāḥ

And there, after passing the terrific sea of red waters called Yellow, you will behold a mighty knarled Salmali. There, built by Visvakarma, peak-like, gigantic, resembling Kailasa, (towere) the mansion of Vinata's offspring. There, grim Raksasas named Mandehas, resembling hills, of diverse shapes, capable of inspiring fear, hang head foremost on the rocks.

ते पतन्ति जले नित्यं सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति
अभितप्ताश्च सूर्येण लम्बन्ते स्म पुनः पुनः

te patanti jale nityaṁ sūryasyodayanaṁ prati
abhitaptāśca sūryeṇa lambante sma punaḥ punaḥ
Day after day at sunrise, these Raksasas heated (by solar rays) and struck dead by Brahma energy,* again and again (hang on the crags). *The commentator explains: energy darted from the three orders.

तस्य मध्ये महाश्वेत ऋषभो नाम पर्वतः
दिव्यगन्धैः कुसुमितै रजतैश्च नगैर्वृतः

tasya madhye mahāśveta ṛṣabho nāma parvataḥ
divyagandhaiḥ kusumitai rajataiśca nagairvṛtaḥ

In it there are the mighty white mountain going by the name of Rsabha, covered with trees bearing odorous blossoms; as well as the tank known under the name of Sudarsana, swarming with swans and shining silver lotuses having golden filaments.

विबुधाश्चारणा यक्षाः किंनराः साप्सरोगणाः
हृष्टाः समभिगच्छन्ति नलिनीं तां रिरंसवः

vibudhāścāraṇā yakṣāḥ kiṁnarāḥ sāpsarogaṇāḥ
hṛṣṭāḥ samabhigacchanti nalinīṁ tāṁ riraṁsavaḥ
Desirous of sport, resort to this tank delighted troops of Vivudhas and Charanas, Yaksas, Kinnaras and Apsaras.

तत्र विक्रोशतां नादो भूतानां सागरौकसाम्
श्रूयते चासमर्थानां दृष्ट्वा तद्वडवामुखम्

tatra vikrośatāṁ nādo bhūtānāṁ sāgaraukasām
śrūyate cāsamarthānāṁ dṛṣṭvā tadvaḍavāmukham

Leaving behind Ksiroda, O monkeys, you will soon after behold the Jaloda sea, striking terror into all beings. There presideth that mighty ireborn Energy of him*. (embodied in) the mouth of a mule. This wondrous (universe) containing mobile and immobile things and fraught with great impetus, is the aliment of this Energy. There are heard the cries of feeble creatures inhabiting the sea, who began to wail on witnessing the mouth of the mule. *Sage Aurvi.

स्वादूदस्योत्तरे देशे योजनानि त्रयोदश
जातरूपशिलो नाम महान्कनकपर्वतः

svādūdasyottare deśe yojanāni trayodaśa
jātarūpaśilo nāma mahānkanakaparvataḥ
On the north of the Swadu sea, lie thirteen Yojanas (of land), named Jatarupasila, * exceeding spacious, and of the splendour of gold. Lit. of gold and stone.

आसीनं पर्वतस्याग्रे सर्वभूतनमस्कृतम्
सहस्रशिरसं देवमनन्तं नीलवाससं

āsīnaṁ parvatasyāgre sarvabhūtanamaskṛtam
sahasraśirasaṁ devamanantaṁ nīlavāsasaṁ

There, you monkeys, you will behold that serpent, the holder of Earth-resembling the moon, and with expansive eyes like lotuspetals-seated at the summit of the mount,-that one worshipped of all deities, having a thousand heads,-the god Ananta, clad in blue apparel.

त्रिशिराः काञ्चनः केतुस्तालस्तस्य महात्मनः
स्थापितः पर्वतस्याग्रे विराजति सवेदिकः

triśirāḥ kāñcanaḥ ketustālastasya mahātmanaḥ
sthāpitaḥ parvatasyāgre virājati savedikaḥ
And by the dais (there) at the top of the mount is the golden palm, planted by that high souled one,—which is like a banner.

पूर्वस्यां दिशि निर्माणं कृतं तत्त्रिदशेश्वरैः
ततः परं हेममयः श्रीमानुदयपर्वतः

pūrvasyāṁ diśi nirmāṇaṁ kṛtaṁ tattridaśeśvaraiḥ
tataḥ paraṁ hemamayaḥ śrīmānudayaparvataḥ
The chief of the celestials reared it in the Eastern region. After that is the fair Rising mountain.

सालैस्तालैस्तमालैश्च कर्णिकारैश्च पुष्पितैः
जातरूपमयैर्दिव्यैः शोभते सूर्यसंनिभैः

sālaistālaistamālaiśca karṇikāraiśca puṣpitaiḥ
jātarūpamayairdivyaiḥ śobhate sūryasaṁnibhaiḥ

Its golden peak measuring a hundred Yojanas, reaching to the heavens, rises nobly, with mountains at its base; and looks beautiful with Salas, palms, Tamalas, and flowering Karnikaras,-golden, splendid and resembling the sun.

तत्र योजनविस्तारमुच्छ्रितं दशयोजनम्
शृङ्गं सौमनसं नाम जातरूपमयं ध्रुवम्

tatra yojanavistāramucchritaṁ daśayojanam
śṛṅgaṁ saumanasaṁ nāma jātarūpamayaṁ dhruvam
There, spreading a Yojana around, towering up ten, is the peak named Saumanasa-all certainly of gold.

तत्र पूर्वं पदं कृत्वा पुरा विष्णुस्त्रिविक्रमे
द्वितीयं शिखरं मेरोश्चकार पुरुषोत्तमः

tatra pūrvaṁ padaṁ kṛtvā purā viṣṇustrivikrame
dvitīyaṁ śikharaṁ meroścakāra puruṣottamaḥ
There, formerly on the occasion of invading the earth with three paces, that foremost of persons, Visnu, planting his first foot planted the other on the summit of Meru.

उत्तरेण परिक्रम्य जम्बूद्वीपं दिवाकरः
दृश्यो भवति भूयिष्ठं शिखरं तन्महोच्छ्रयम्

uttareṇa parikramya jambūdvīpaṁ divākaraḥ
dṛśyo bhavati bhūyiṣṭhaṁ śikharaṁ tanmahocchrayam
The sun, having passed by Jambudwipa on the north, and, arriving at that mighty and eminent summit, (Saumanasa), again becomes visible to the dwellers of Jambudwipa.

अयं सुदर्शनो द्वीपः पुरो यस्य प्रकाशते
यस्मिंस्तेजश्च चक्षुश्च सर्वप्रानभृतामपि

ayaṁ sudarśano dvīpaḥ puro yasya prakāśate
yasmiṁstejaśca cakṣuśca sarvaprānabhṛtāmapi
This is the island of Sudarsana, before which all creatures inspire energy and have their sight granted to them.

शैलस्य तस्य कुञ्जेषु कन्दरेषु वनेषु च
रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः

śailasya tasya kuñjeṣu kandareṣu vaneṣu ca
rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyastatastataḥ
You should search for Ravana with Vaidehi all round the top of that mountain as well as in its forests and woods.

काञ्चनस्य च शैलस्य सूर्यस्य च महात्मनः
आविष्टा तेजसा संध्या पूर्वा रक्ता प्रकाशते

kāñcanasya ca śailasya sūryasya ca mahātmanaḥ
āviṣṭā tejasā saṁdhyā pūrvā raktā prakāśate
(Here) the first twilight enfolded in the glory of the golden hill and that of the high-souled Sun, appeareth roseate.

ततः परमगम्या स्याद्दिक्पूर्वा त्रिदशावृता
रहिता चन्द्रसूर्याभ्यामदृश्या तिमिरावृता

tataḥ paramagamyā syāddikpūrvā tridaśāvṛtā
rahitā candrasūryābhyāmadṛśyā timirāvṛtā
Beyond that, is the exceedingly impassable Eastern quarter, thronged by the celestials, covered with darkness and devoid of the sun and the moon.

शैलेषु तेषु सर्वेषु कन्दरेषु वनेषु च
ये च नोक्ता मया देशा विचेया तेषु जानकी

śaileṣu teṣu sarveṣu kandareṣu vaneṣu ca
ye ca noktā mayā deśā viceyā teṣu jānakī
Do you search for Janaki in all those rocks, woods and streams as well as in such spots as I have not mentioned.

एतावद्वानरैः शक्यं गन्तुं वानरपुंगवाः
अभास्करममर्यादं न जानीमस्ततः परम्

etāvadvānaraiḥ śakyaṁ gantuṁ vānarapuṁgavāḥ
abhāskaramamaryādaṁ na jānīmastataḥ param
You foremost of monkeys, the monkeys are competent to proceed thus far. Beyond this, of the tract without sun and without limit, I know nothing.

अधिगम्य तु वैदेहीं निलयं रावणस्य च
मासे पूर्णे निवर्तध्वमुदयं प्राप्य पर्वतम्

adhigamya tu vaidehīṁ nilayaṁ rāvaṇasya ca
māse pūrṇe nivartadhvamudayaṁ prāpya parvatam
Meeting with Vaidehi and arriving at) Ravana's mansion, do you, having reached the Rising hill, turn back, when it shall be a full month.

ऊर्ध्वं मासान्न वस्तव्यं वसन्वध्यो भवेन्मम
सिद्धार्थाः संनिवर्तध्वमधिगम्य च मैथिलीम्

ūrdhvaṁ māsānna vastavyaṁ vasanvadhyo bhavenmama
siddhārthāḥ saṁnivartadhvamadhigamya ca maithilīm
Do not stay longer than a month. If you do, you shall be slain by me. Having attained your end, do you turn back, having met with Maithili.

महेन्द्रकान्तां वनषण्ड मण्डितां; दिशं चरित्वा निपुणेन वानराः
अवाप्य सीतां रघुवंशजप्रियां; ततो निवृत्ताः सुखितो भविष्यथ

mahendrakāntāṁ vanaṣaṇḍa maṇḍitāṁ; diśaṁ caritvā nipuṇena vānarāḥ
avāpya sītāṁ raghuvaṁśajapriyāṁ; tato nivṛttāḥ sukhito bhaviṣyatha
Having adroitly explored (the tract) loved of Mahendra, plated with woods, do you, you monkeys, having come at Sita—the beloved wife of that descendant of Raghu-desist, attaining happiness.

ततः प्रस्थाप्य सुग्रीवस्तन्महद्वानरं बलम्
दक्षिणां प्रेषयामास वानरानभिलक्षितान्

tataḥ prasthāpya sugrīvastanmahadvānaraṁ balam
dakṣiṇāṁ preṣayāmāsa vānarānabhilakṣitān
Then having sent away that mighty host of monkeys, Sugriva despatched to the South others competent to perform the several tasks entrusted to them.

विचित्रशिखरः श्रीमांश्चित्रपुष्पितकाननः
सचन्दनवनोद्देशो मार्गितव्यो महागिरिः

vicitraśikharaḥ śrīmāṁścitrapuṣpitakānanaḥ
sacandanavanoddeśo mārgitavyo mahāgiriḥ

Then shall you repair to the mountain Ayomukha,* plated with ore, having taking summits, graceful, furnished with picturesque flowering woods,-the mighty mountain having groves of excellent sandal. *Another name of this hill is Malaya.

ततस्तामापगां दिव्यां प्रसन्नसलिलां शिवाम्
तत्र द्रक्ष्यथ कावेरीं विहृतामप्सरोगणैः

tatastāmāpagāṁ divyāṁ prasannasalilāṁ śivām
tatra drakṣyatha kāverīṁ vihṛtāmapsarogaṇaiḥ
At the foot of the Malaya mountain endued with exceeding energy, you will behold the noble stream Kaveri, of pleasant waters, where sport troops of Apsaras.

तस्यासीनं नगस्याग्रे मलयस्य महौजसं
द्रक्ष्यथादित्यसंकाशमगस्त्यमृषिसत्तमम्

tasyāsīnaṁ nagasyāgre malayasya mahaujasaṁ
drakṣyathādityasaṁkāśamagastyamṛṣisattamam
(There) you will see that foremost of saints, Agastya, resembling the sun.

ततस्तेनाभ्यनुज्ञाताः प्रसन्नेन महात्मना
ताम्रपर्णीं ग्राहजुष्टां तरिष्यथ महानदीम्

tatastenābhyanujñātāḥ prasannena mahātmanā
tāmraparṇīṁ grāhajuṣṭāṁ tariṣyatha mahānadīm
Permitted by that gratified high-souled one, you will cross over the great river, Taniraparni, abounding in alligators.

सा चन्दनवनैर्दिव्यैः प्रच्छन्ना द्वीप शालिनी
कान्तेव युवतिः कान्तं समुद्रमवगाहते

sā candanavanairdivyaiḥ pracchannā dvīpa śālinī
kānteva yuvatiḥ kāntaṁ samudramavagāhate
Like a youthful female in relation to her lover, she (Tamraparni), with both her waters as well as islets concealed under beautiful sandal woods, bathes in the sea.

ततो हेममयं दिव्यं मुक्तामणिविभूषितम्
युक्तं कवाटं पाण्ड्यानां गता द्रक्ष्यथ वानराः

tato hemamayaṁ divyaṁ muktāmaṇivibhūṣitam
yuktaṁ kavāṭaṁ pāṇḍyānāṁ gatā drakṣyatha vānarāḥ
Proceeding (therefrom), the monkeys shall see the grand golden gates belonging to the walls of the capital of the Pandyas.

ततः समुद्रमासाद्य संप्रधार्यार्थनिश्चयम्
अगस्त्येनान्तरे तत्र सागरे विनिवेशितः

tataḥ samudramāsādya saṁpradhāryārthaniścayam
agastyenāntare tatra sāgare viniveśitaḥ

Then arriving at the main, you shall ascertain your ability or otherwise of crossing the same. In the bosom of the deep there, Agastya has placed that foremost of mountains-the charming Mahendra, having picturesque plateaus; golden, and beautiful,-with a portion of it sunk in the great ocean.

नानाविधैर्नगैः फुल्लैर्लताभिश्चोपशोभितम्
देवर्षियक्षप्रवरैरप्सरोभिश्च सेवितम्

nānāvidhairnagaiḥ phullairlatābhiścopaśobhitam
devarṣiyakṣapravarairapsarobhiśca sevitam

For aye, He of a thousand eyes at Parvas visiteth this mountain embellished by various blossoming trees and creepers; beauteous with divinities, and saints, and the foremost Yaksas and Apsaras; thronged by numbers of Siddhas and Charanas; and of surpassing loveliness.

द्वीपस्तस्यापरे पारे शतयोजनमायतः
अगम्यो मानुषैर्दीप्तस्तं मार्गध्वं समन्ततः
तत्र सर्वात्मना सीता मार्गितव्या विशेषतः

dvīpastasyāpare pāre śatayojanamāyataḥ
agamyo mānuṣairdīptastaṁ mārgadhvaṁ samantataḥ
tatra sarvātmanā sītā mārgitavyā viśeṣataḥ

On its other shore is an island extending over an hundred Yojanas, inaccessible to men*, and of splendid aspect. Do you explore it all round. There, in particular, you must every way search for Sita. *Because, says the commentator,. of the profusion of gold in it.

स हि देशस्तु वध्यस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः
राक्षसाधिपतेर्वासः सहस्राक्षसमद्युतेः

sa hi deśastu vadhyasya rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
rākṣasādhipatervāsaḥ sahasrākṣasamadyuteḥ
That country belongs to the impious Ravana, worthy of being slain—the lord of Raksasas, like to the thousand-eyed (deity) in splendour.

दक्षिणस्य समुद्रस्य मध्ये तस्य तु राक्षसी
अङ्गारकेति विख्याता छायामाक्षिप्य भोजिनी

dakṣiṇasya samudrasya madhye tasya tu rākṣasī
aṅgāraketi vikhyātā chāyāmākṣipya bhojinī
In the midst of the Southern sea belonging to him (Ravana), there is a Raksasi, named Angaraketi, who procureth her pray by casting her shadow.

तमतिक्रम्य लक्ष्मीवान्समुद्रे शतयोजने
गिरिः पुष्पितको नाम सिद्धचारणसेवितः

tamatikramya lakṣmīvānsamudre śatayojane
giriḥ puṣpitako nāma siddhacāraṇasevitaḥ

In the sea extending over an hundred Yojanas, a lovely hill, named Puspitaka, the abode of Siddhas and Charanas; resembling the rays of the sun or the moon,-resting on the waters of the ocean, looks splendid, piercing the heavens with its giant peaks. Of this (mountain), there is a particular golden summit, which the sun approaches. It is incapable of being beheld by the ungrateful or the atheistical.

तत्र योजनविस्तारमुच्छ्रितं दशयोजनम्
शरणं काञ्चनं दिव्यं नानारत्नविभूषितम्

tatra yojanavistāramucchritaṁ daśayojanam
śaraṇaṁ kāñcanaṁ divyaṁ nānāratnavibhūṣitam

There is the hill named Kunjara, grateful both to the eye and the mind, where Visvakarma had built the abode of Agastya*. There (rises) that stately golden pile, adorned with various gems, extending over one Yojana, and ten in height. *i.e. in that hill.

तत्र भोगवती नाम सर्पाणामालयः पुरी
विशालरथ्या दुर्धर्षा सर्वतः परिरक्षिता
रक्षिता पन्नगैर्घोरैस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रैर्महाविषैः

tatra bhogavatī nāma sarpāṇāmālayaḥ purī
viśālarathyā durdharṣā sarvataḥ parirakṣitā
rakṣitā pannagairghoraistīkṣṇadaṁṣṭrairmahāviṣaiḥ

In it also there is that palace, which is the abode of snakes; having spacious ways, i incapable of being captured, guarded around, and protected by dreadful snakes and sharptoothed serpents of virulent poison; where dwelleth Vasuki, the exceedingly terrible king of snakes. Proceeding heedfully, you must explore that Bhogavati palace; also whatever concealed place may lie there.

अन्ते पृथिव्या दुर्धर्षास्तत्र स्वर्गजितः स्थिताः
ततः परं न वः सेव्यः पितृलोकः सुदारुणः
राजधानी यमस्यैषा कष्टेन तमसावृता

ante pṛthivyā durdharṣāstatra svargajitaḥ sthitāḥ
tataḥ paraṁ na vaḥ sevyaḥ pitṛlokaḥ sudāruṇaḥ
rājadhānī yamasyaiṣā kaṣṭena tamasāvṛtā

And there reside persons who have won the heavenly regions. After that are the awful regions of the ancestral manes, which you must not approach. This is the metropolis of Yama, covered by deep gloom.

एतावदेव युष्माभिर्वीरा वानरपुंगवाः
शक्यं विचेतुं गन्तुं वा नातो गतिमतां गतिः

etāvadeva yuṣmābhirvīrā vānarapuṁgavāḥ
śakyaṁ vicetuṁ gantuṁ vā nāto gatimatāṁ gatiḥ
You heroic monkey chiefs, you can seek thus far. Further there is no course for those endued with motion.

सर्वमेतत्समालोक्य यच्चान्यदपि दृश्यते
गतिं विदित्वा वैदेह्याः संनिवर्तितमर्हथ

sarvametatsamālokya yaccānyadapi dṛśyate
gatiṁ viditvā vaidehyāḥ saṁnivartitamarhatha
Having examined all these, as well others that may come within your ken, it behoves you, after having ascertained Vaidehi's course, to return (hither).

यस्तु मासान्निवृत्तोऽग्रे दृष्टा सीतेति वक्ष्यति
मत्तुल्यविभवो भोगैः सुखं स विहरिष्यति

yastu māsānnivṛtto'gre dṛṣṭā sīteti vakṣyati
mattulyavibhavo bhogaiḥ sukhaṁ sa vihariṣyati
He that, returning within a month, shall say,—I have seen Sita,' shall pass his days in happiness, enjoying affluence like mine own and indulging all pleasures.

ततः प्रियतरो नास्ति मम प्राणाद्विशेषतः
कृतापराधो बहुशो मम बन्धुर्भविष्यति

tataḥ priyataro nāsti mama prāṇādviśeṣataḥ
kṛtāparādho bahuśo mama bandhurbhaviṣyati
He shall be dearer to me than life itself, and none dearer (to me) that he; and although he might commit innumerable wrongs, still should he become my friend.

अमितबलपराक्रमा भवन्तो; विपुलगुणेषु कुलेषु च प्रसूताः
मनुजपतिसुतां यथा लभध्वं; तदधिगुणं पुरुषार्थमारभध्वम्

amitabalaparākramā bhavanto; vipulaguṇeṣu kuleṣu ca prasūtāḥ
manujapatisutāṁ yathā labhadhvaṁ; tadadhiguṇaṁ puruṣārthamārabhadhvam

Possessed of immeasurable strength and prowess, and sprung from lines crowned with sterling virtues, do you strive manfully in such a glorious way that the king's daughter may be recovered. prowess, and sprung from lines crowned with sterling virtues, do you strive manfully in such a glorious way that the king's daughter may be recovered.

गिरिजालावृतां दुर्गां मार्गित्वा पश्चिमां दिशम्
ततः पश्चिममासाद्य समुद्रं द्रष्टुमर्हथ
तिमि नक्रायुत जलमक्षोभ्यमथ वानरः

girijālāvṛtāṁ durgāṁ mārgitvā paścimāṁ diśam
tataḥ paścimamāsādya samudraṁ draṣṭumarhatha
timi nakrāyuta jalamakṣobhyamatha vānaraḥ

There having explored tracts resembling deserts, and cold cliffs towering high, and the West, covered with mountain ranges, and extremely difficult of access,-and proceeding at a little more to the west, it behoves you a view of the sea. And proceeding on, you monkeys, you shall see (the ocean), whose waters abound in whales and alligators, you monkeys.* Then the apes shall sport in tracts covered by Ketakas, and dense with Tamalas and woods of coconuts. There shall you look for $ita and the mansion of Ravana, *The grammar of these slokas is exceedingly vicious; and it has cost the Translator no small amount of labour to assign the necessary logical nexus in a good many praces:

अवन्तीमङ्गलोपां च तथा चालक्षितं वनम्
राष्ट्राणि च विशालानि पत्तनानि ततस्ततः

avantīmaṅgalopāṁ ca tathā cālakṣitaṁ vanam
rāṣṭrāṇi ca viśālāni pattanāni tatastataḥ

In hills and woods on the shores of the sea; and (explore) Muracipattana, and the delightful Jatapura, and Avanti, and Angalepa, as well as in the wood (called) Alaksita, and spacious monarchies, and emporiums.

तस्य प्रस्थेषु रम्येषु सिंहाः पक्षगमाः स्थिताः
तिमिमत्स्यगजांश्चैव नीडान्यारोपयन्ति ते

tasya prastheṣu ramyeṣu siṁhāḥ pakṣagamāḥ sthitāḥ
timimatsyagajāṁścaiva nīḍānyāropayanti te

There is a mighty mountain where the Sindhu falls into the sea, Somagiri by name; having an hundred summits and tall trees. In its plateaus there are certain birds (called) Sinhas. These lift up to their nests whales and elephants.

तानि नीडानि सिंहानां गिरिशृङ्गगताश्च ये
दृप्तास्तृप्ताश्च मातङ्गास्तोयदस्वननिःस्वनाः
विचरन्ति विशालेऽस्मिंस्तोयपूर्णे समन्ततः

tāni nīḍāni siṁhānāṁ giriśṛṅgagatāśca ye
dṛptāstṛptāśca mātaṅgāstoyadasvananiḥsvanāḥ
vicaranti viśāle'smiṁstoyapūrṇe samantataḥ

The proud elephants carried to the nests and remaining on the summits of the mountain, possessing the roar of clouds, having been gratified (with food), range around this extensive table-land filled with water.

तस्य शृङ्गं दिवस्पर्शं काञ्चनं चित्रपादपम्
सर्वमाशु विचेतव्यं कपिभिः कामरूपिभिः

tasya śṛṅgaṁ divasparśaṁ kāñcanaṁ citrapādapam
sarvamāśu vicetavyaṁ kapibhiḥ kāmarūpibhiḥ
The monkeys, capable of wearing shapes at will, should swiftly search its golden summit towering to the sky and filled with graceful trees.

कोटिं तत्र समुद्रे तु काञ्चनीं शतयोजनम्
दुर्दर्शां परियात्रस्य गता द्रक्ष्यथ वानराः

koṭiṁ tatra samudre tu kāñcanīṁ śatayojanam
durdarśāṁ pariyātrasya gatā drakṣyatha vānarāḥ
Proceeding further, the monkeys shall behold the golden summit of Pariyatra rising from the sea and extending over an hundred Yojanas.

कोट्यस्तत्र चतुर्विंशद्गन्धर्वाणां तरस्विनाम्
वसन्त्यग्निनिकाशानां घोराणां कामरूपिणाम्

koṭyastatra caturviṁśadgandharvāṇāṁ tarasvinām
vasantyagninikāśānāṁ ghorāṇāṁ kāmarūpiṇām
There dwell all around in a body four and twenty kotis of ascetic Gandharvas, resembling fire, dreadful, practicising impiety, and like to flames of fire.

नात्यासादयितव्यास्ते वानरैर्भीमविक्रमैः
नादेयं च फलं तस्माद्देशात्किंचित्प्लवंगमैः

nātyāsādayitavyāste vānarairbhīmavikramaiḥ
nādeyaṁ ca phalaṁ tasmāddeśātkiṁcitplavaṁgamaiḥ
The monkeys of dreadful prowess should not present themselves before those, nor should they take any fruits from that country.

दुरासदा हि ते वीराः सत्त्ववन्तो महाबलाः
फलमूलानि ते तत्र रक्षन्ते भीमविक्रमाः

durāsadā hi te vīrāḥ sattvavanto mahābalāḥ
phalamūlāni te tatra rakṣante bhīmavikramāḥ
Those heroes are hard to approach; and they are truthful and possessed of great might. And there they of dreadful prowess stow away their fruits and roots.

तत्र यत्नश्च कर्तव्यो मार्गितव्या च जानकी
न हि तेभ्यो भयं किंचित्कपित्वमनुवर्तताम्

tatra yatnaśca kartavyo mārgitavyā ca jānakī
na hi tebhyo bhayaṁ kiṁcitkapitvamanuvartatām
There you should heedfully search for Janaki. you have no fear whatever from them; do you only follow your native nature as monkeys.

चतुर्भागे समुद्रस्य चक्रवान्नाम पर्वतः
तत्र चक्रं सहस्रारं निर्मितं विश्वकर्मणा

caturbhāge samudrasya cakravānnāma parvataḥ
tatra cakraṁ sahasrāraṁ nirmitaṁ viśvakarmaṇā
On the fourth side of the Ocean is a mountain named Cakravan. There Visvakarma forged the discus (called) Sahasrara.

तत्र पञ्चजनं हत्वा हयग्रीवं च दानवम्
आजहार ततश्चक्रं शङ्खं च पुरुषोत्तमः

tatra pañcajanaṁ hatvā hayagrīvaṁ ca dānavam
ājahāra tataścakraṁ śaṅkhaṁ ca puruṣottamaḥ
There, slaying Panchajana and the Danava, Hayagriva*, the best of male beings obtained the discus as well as the conch. *Lit. horse-necked.

तस्य सानुषु चित्रेषु विशालासु गुहासु च
रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः

tasya sānuṣu citreṣu viśālāsu guhāsu ca
rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyastatastataḥ
There do you everywhere search for Ravana along with Vaidehi in the beautiful plateaus and huge caves.

योजनानि चतुःषष्टिर्वराहो नाम पर्वतः
सुवर्णशृङ्गः सुश्रीमानगाधे वरुणालये

yojanāni catuḥṣaṣṭirvarāho nāma parvataḥ
suvarṇaśṛṅgaḥ suśrīmānagādhe varuṇālaye
Sunk in the depths of the sea, is a very great mountain named Varaha, having golden peaks and measuring four and sixty yojanas.

तत्र प्राग्ज्योतिषं नाम जातरूपमयं पुरम्
यस्मिन्वस्ति दुष्टात्मा नरको नाम गुहासु च

tatra prāgjyotiṣaṁ nāma jātarūpamayaṁ puram
yasminvasti duṣṭātmā narako nāma guhāsu ca
In it is a city named Pragjyotisa, all of gold. There dwells the wicked Danava named Naraka.* *i.e. in the Varadha hill.

तस्य सानुषु चित्रेषु विशालासु गुहासु च
रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः

tasya sānuṣu citreṣu viśālāsu guhāsu ca
rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyastatastataḥ
In those beautiful plateous and huge caves, you should everywhere search for Ravana with Videha's daughter.

तमतिक्रम्य शैलेन्द्रं काञ्चनान्तरनिर्दरः
पर्वतः सर्वसौवर्णो धारा प्रस्रवणायुतः

tamatikramya śailendraṁ kāñcanāntaranirdaraḥ
parvataḥ sarvasauvarṇo dhārā prasravaṇāyutaḥ

Passing beyond that foremost of mountains, whose sight betrays the secret of its bowels being freighted with gold, (you shall come upon) the mountain Sarvasauvarna, furnished with fountains and cascades.

तं गजाश्च वराहाश्च सिंहा व्याघ्राश्च सर्वतः
अभिगर्जन्ति सततं तेन शब्देन दर्पिताः

taṁ gajāśca varāhāśca siṁhā vyāghrāśca sarvataḥ
abhigarjanti satataṁ tena śabdena darpitāḥ
Coming to it, elephants, and boars, and lions, and tigers, on all sides roar ceaselessly, wrought up by the echoes their own cries have produced.

तस्मिन्हरिहयः श्रीमान्महेन्द्रः पाकशासनः
अभिषिक्तः सुरै राजा मेघवान्नाम पर्वतः

tasminharihayaḥ śrīmānmahendraḥ pākaśāsanaḥ
abhiṣiktaḥ surai rājā meghavānnāma parvataḥ
This is the mountain named Megha, where the graceful green-horsed vanquisher of Paka, Mahendra, was installed king by the gods.

तरुणादित्यवर्णानि भ्राजमानानि सर्वतः
जातरूपमयैर्वृक्षैः शोभितानि सुपुष्पितैः

taruṇādityavarṇāni bhrājamānāni sarvataḥ
jātarūpamayairvṛkṣaiḥ śobhitāni supuṣpitaiḥ

Having passed by that mountain protected by Mahendra, you shall repair to sixty thousand hills of gold; in hue like the infant sun, and blazing on all sides and embellished by blossoming golden trees,

तेनैवमुक्तः शैलेन्द्रः सर्व एव त्वदाश्रयाः
मत्प्रसादाद्भविष्यन्ति दिवारात्रौ च काञ्चनाः

tenaivamuktaḥ śailendraḥ sarva eva tvadāśrayāḥ
matprasādādbhaviṣyanti divārātrau ca kāñcanāḥ

In the midst of them is established as king, Meru, best of mountains, formerly the Sun being well pleased, conferred a boon on this mountain, and he addressed the mountain, saying,—'By my grace all the hills that are under your protection, shall be golden day and night; and also those gods Gandharvas and Danvas that shall dwell in you, shall be filled with reverence for me and to the boot attain a golden glory.'

आदित्यमुपतिष्ठन्ति तैश्च सूर्योऽभिपूजितः
अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानामस्तं गच्छति पर्वतम्

ādityamupatiṣṭhanti taiśca sūryo'bhipūjitaḥ
adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāmastaṁ gacchati parvatam

Coming to the excellent mountain Meru. Visvadevas, the Vasus, the Maruts and the celestials, adore the Sun in the western twilight. Adored by them, the Sun, becoming invisible, repaireth to the Setting hill*. The commentator remarks: Although not expressly stated, it is implied that the islands to the west of it are also to be searched.

योजनानां सहस्राणि दशतानि दिवाकरः
मुहूर्तार्धेन तं शीघ्रमभियाति शिलोच्चयम्

yojanānāṁ sahasrāṇi daśatāni divākaraḥ
muhūrtārdhena taṁ śīghramabhiyāti śiloccayam
In half a muhurta, the Sun swiftly passes over this (mountain), measuring, as it does, ten thousand Yojanas.

शोभितं तरुभिश्चित्रैर्नानापक्षिसमाकुलैः
निकेतं पाशहस्तस्य वरुणस्य महात्मनः

śobhitaṁ tarubhiścitrairnānāpakṣisamākulaiḥ
niketaṁ pāśahastasya varuṇasya mahātmanaḥ

On its peak rises an edifice; resembling the sun (in splendour); consisting of palatial mansions built by Visvakarma; and graced by goodly trees rife with various birds,-the residence of the high-souled Varuna, bearing the noose in his hand.

अन्तरा मेरुमस्तं च तालो दशशिरा महान्
जातरूपमयः श्रीमान्भ्राजते चित्रवेदिकः

antarā merumastaṁ ca tālo daśaśirā mahān
jātarūpamayaḥ śrīmānbhrājate citravedikaḥ
Between Meru and the Setting hill, towers a tall palm having ten heads. Golden and graceful, it shineth on a variegated dais.

तेषु सर्वेषु दुर्गेषु सरःसु च सरित्सु च
रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः

teṣu sarveṣu durgeṣu saraḥsu ca saritsu ca
rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyastatastataḥ
In all these, difficult of access, as also in rivers and tanks, you should thoroughly search for Ravana along with Vaidehi.

यत्र तिष्ठति धर्मात्मा तपसा स्वेन भावितः
मेरुसावर्णिरित्येव ख्यातो वै ब्रह्मणा समः

yatra tiṣṭhati dharmātmā tapasā svena bhāvitaḥ
merusāvarṇirityeva khyāto vai brahmaṇā samaḥ
There dwells there the righteous and famous Merusavarani, sanctified by virtue of his own ascesticism, and like to Brahma himself*. *Like to Prajapati dwelling by Mahameru.

प्रष्टव्यो मेरुसावर्णिर्महर्षिः सूर्यसंनिभः
प्रणम्य शिरसा भूमौ प्रवृत्तिं मैथिलीं प्रति

praṣṭavyo merusāvarṇirmaharṣiḥ sūryasaṁnibhaḥ
praṇamya śirasā bhūmau pravṛttiṁ maithilīṁ prati
Bowing down your heads to the earth, you should ask the Maharsi Merusavarni, resembling the sun, touching Mithila's daughter.

एतावज्जीवलोकस्य भास्करो रजनीक्षये
कृत्वा वितिमिरं सर्वमस्तं गच्छति पर्वतम्

etāvajjīvalokasya bhāskaro rajanīkṣaye
kṛtvā vitimiraṁ sarvamastaṁ gacchati parvatam
On the departure of night, the sun dispels the darkness of the world to this extent, and then enters the Setting hill.

एतावद्वानरैः शक्यं गन्तुं वानरपुंगवाः
अभास्करममर्यादं न जानीमस्ततः परम्

etāvadvānaraiḥ śakyaṁ gantuṁ vānarapuṁgavāḥ
abhāskaramamaryādaṁ na jānīmastataḥ param
You foremost of monkeys, the monkeys are able to proceed thus far. Beyond this, of what is sunless and boundless I know nothing.

अधिगम्य तु वैदेहीं निलयं रावणस्य च
अस्तं पर्वतमासाद्य पूर्णे मासे निवर्तत

adhigamya tu vaidehīṁ nilayaṁ rāvaṇasya ca
astaṁ parvatamāsādya pūrṇe māse nivartata
Having come to Vaidehi and Ravana's mansions, and arrived at the Setting-hill, do you return of the month being complete.

ऊर्ध्वं मासान्न वस्तव्यं वसन्वध्यो भवेन्मम
सहैव शूरो युष्माभिः श्वशुरो मे गमिष्यति

ūrdhvaṁ māsānna vastavyaṁ vasanvadhyo bhavenmama
sahaiva śūro yuṣmābhiḥ śvaśuro me gamiṣyati
You must not stay above a month; and if you do, you must be slain by me. And along with you goeth that hero, my father-in-law.

श्रोतव्यं सर्वमेतस्य भवद्भिर्दिष्ट कारिभिः
गुरुरेष महाबाहुः श्वशुरो मे महाबलः

śrotavyaṁ sarvametasya bhavadbhirdiṣṭa kāribhiḥ
gurureṣa mahābāhuḥ śvaśuro me mahābalaḥ
You, abiding by his orders, should listen to all that he sayeth. My mighty-armed father-in-law, gifted with great strength, is my spiritual preceptor.

भवन्तश्चापि विक्रान्ताः प्रमाणं सर्वकर्मसु
प्रमाणमेनं संस्थाप्य पश्यध्वं पश्चिमां दिशम्

bhavantaścāpi vikrāntāḥ pramāṇaṁ sarvakarmasu
pramāṇamenaṁ saṁsthāpya paśyadhvaṁ paścimāṁ diśam

All of you possessed of prowess, yourselves certainly constitute the measure whereby to ascertain the wisdom or otherwise of a course. Making this one also into a measure, survey the western quarter. Having requited the good that has been done to us, we shall attain our end.

अतोऽन्यदपि यत्किंचित्कार्यस्यास्य हितं भवेत्
संप्रधार्य भवद्भिश्च देशकालार्थसंहितम्

ato'nyadapi yatkiṁcitkāryasyāsya hitaṁ bhavet
saṁpradhārya bhavadbhiśca deśakālārthasaṁhitam
De you also determine what else is agreeable (to Rama), and in consonance with place, season and profit, should be performed by you in the matter of this business.

ततः सुषेण प्रमुखाः प्लवंगमाः; सुग्रीववाक्यं निपुणं निशम्य
आमन्त्र्य सर्वे प्लवगाधिपं ते; जग्मुर्दिशं तां वरुणाभिगुप्ताम्

tataḥ suṣeṇa pramukhāḥ plavaṁgamāḥ; sugrīvavākyaṁ nipuṇaṁ niśamya
āmantrya sarve plavagādhipaṁ te; jagmurdiśaṁ tāṁ varuṇābhiguptām
Then those monkeys-the monkey-chiefs headed by Susena, having heard Sugriva's deft speech, set out for the quarter protected by Varuna.

ततः संदिश्य सुग्रीवः श्वशुरं पश्चिमां दिशम्
वीरं शतबलिं नाम वानरं वानरर्षभः

tataḥ saṁdiśya sugrīvaḥ śvaśuraṁ paścimāṁ diśam
vīraṁ śatabaliṁ nāma vānaraṁ vānararṣabhaḥ

Having directed his father-in-law to proceed to the West, that best to monkeys, the allknowing king Sugriva, lord of apes, then spoke to the heroic monkey, named Satavala, words fraught with good to himself as well as to Rama,

वृतः शतसहस्रेण त्वद्विधानां वनौकसाम्
वैवस्वत सुतैः सार्धं प्रतिष्ठस्व स्वमन्त्रिभिः

vṛtaḥ śatasahasreṇa tvadvidhānāṁ vanaukasām
vaivasvata sutaiḥ sārdhaṁ pratiṣṭhasva svamantribhiḥ

Surrounded by hundreds and thousands of rangers of the forest like yourself, in company with the offspring of Yama as well as the counsellors in a body, do you, O you possessed of prowess, entering the northern quarter furnished with the Himasaila, search everywhere for the illustrious spouse of Rama.

अस्मिन्कार्ये विनिवृत्ते कृते दाशरथेः प्रिये
ऋणान्मुक्ता भविष्यामः कृतार्थार्थविदां वराः

asminkārye vinivṛtte kṛte dāśaratheḥ priye
ṛṇānmuktā bhaviṣyāmaḥ kṛtārthārthavidāṁ varāḥ
Having performed this task satisfactorily, and brought about what is dear to Dasaratha's son, we shall, O best of those that achieve success, be freed from our debts.

कृतं हि प्रियमस्माकं राघवेण महात्मना
तस्य चेत्प्रतिकारोऽस्ति सफलं जीवितं भवेत्

kṛtaṁ hi priyamasmākaṁ rāghaveṇa mahātmanā
tasya cetpratikāro'sti saphalaṁ jīvitaṁ bhavet
The high-souled Raghava had done us good. If we can serve him in turn, our life shall be crowned with success.

एतां बुद्धिं समास्थाय दृश्यते जानकी यथा
तथा भवद्भिः कर्तव्यमस्मत्प्रियहितैषिभिः

etāṁ buddhiṁ samāsthāya dṛśyate jānakī yathā
tathā bhavadbhiḥ kartavyamasmatpriyahitaiṣibhiḥ
Pondering this, those that are engaged in our welfare, should so act that Janaki may be discovered.

अयं हि सर्वभूतानां मान्यस्तु नरसत्तमः
अस्मासु चागतप्रीती रामः परपुरंजयः

ayaṁ hi sarvabhūtānāṁ mānyastu narasattamaḥ
asmāsu cāgataprītī rāmaḥ parapuraṁjayaḥ
And this foremost of men is worthy of being honoured by all creatures; and Ramacaptor of hostile capitals—has also found delight in us.

इमानि वनदुर्गाणि नद्यः शैलान्तराणि च
भवन्तः परिमार्गंस्तु बुद्धिविक्रमसंपदा

imāni vanadurgāṇi nadyaḥ śailāntarāṇi ca
bhavantaḥ parimārgaṁstu buddhivikramasaṁpadā
Endowed with sense and prowess, do you explore these many inaccessible places, rivers and mountains.

तत्र म्लेच्छान्पुलिन्दांश्च शूरसेनांस्तथैव च
प्रस्थालान्भरतांश्चैव कुरूंश्च सह मद्रकैः

tatra mlecchānpulindāṁśca śūrasenāṁstathaiva ca
prasthālānbharatāṁścaiva kurūṁśca saha madrakaiḥ
Having searched there Mlechas, Pulindas, Surasensas, Prasthalas, Bharatas, Kurus, and Madrakas, and Varadas, as well as the cities of Kambojas, Yavanas and Sakas, do you explore Himavan.

लोध्रपद्मकषण्डेषु देवदारुवनेषु च
रावणः सह वैदेह्य मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः

lodhrapadmakaṣaṇḍeṣu devadāruvaneṣu ca
rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehya mārgitavyastatastataḥ
And in tracts of Lodhras and Padmakas, and in Devadaru woods* do you search thoroughly for Ravana along with Videha's daughter. *Belonging, according to the commentator, to Himavan.

ततः सोमाश्रमं गत्वा देवगन्धर्वसेवितम्
कालं नाम महासानुं पर्वतं तं गमिष्यथ

tataḥ somāśramaṁ gatvā devagandharvasevitam
kālaṁ nāma mahāsānuṁ parvataṁ taṁ gamiṣyatha
Then, coming upon the hermitage of Soma, frequented by gods and Gandharvas, do you repair to the mountain called kala possessing spacious plateaus,

महत्सु तस्य शृङ्गेषु निर्दरेषु गुहासु च
विचिनुध्वं महाभागां रामपत्नीं यशस्विनीम्

mahatsu tasya śṛṅgeṣu nirdareṣu guhāsu ca
vicinudhvaṁ mahābhāgāṁ rāmapatnīṁ yaśasvinīm
In those mighty mountains, as also in others and in their caves, do you search for that exalted lady, the blameless wife of Rama.

तमतिक्रम्य शैलेन्द्रं हेमवर्गं महागिरिम्
ततः सुदर्शनं नाम पर्वतं गन्तुमर्हथ

tamatikramya śailendraṁ hemavargaṁ mahāgirim
tataḥ sudarśanaṁ nāma parvataṁ gantumarhatha
Having passed beyond that mighty mountain containing gold in its womb, it behoves you to go to the mountain called Sudarsana.

तस्य काननषण्डेषु निर्दरेषु गुहासु च
रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः

tasya kānanaṣaṇḍeṣu nirdareṣu guhāsu ca
rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyastatastataḥ
In its golden tracts, fountains and caves, do you search for Ravana along with Videha's daughter.

तमतिक्रम्य चाकाशं सर्वतः शतयोजनम्
अपर्वतनदी वृक्षं सर्वसत्त्वविवर्जितम्

tamatikramya cākāśaṁ sarvataḥ śatayojanam
aparvatanadī vṛkṣaṁ sarvasattvavivarjitam
Going beyond it, (you come upon) a vacant land, measuring an hundred Yojanas, without mountains, or rivers, or trees; and void of all living beings.

तं तु शीघ्रमतिक्रम्य कान्तारं रोमहर्षणम्
कैलासं पाण्डुरं शैलं प्राप्य हृष्टा भविष्यथ

taṁ tu śīghramatikramya kāntāraṁ romaharṣaṇam
kailāsaṁ pāṇḍuraṁ śailaṁ prāpya hṛṣṭā bhaviṣyatha
Speedily passing that desert land capable of making one's hair stand on end, you shall feel delighted, on coming to the pale Kailasa.

विशाला नलिनी यत्र प्रभूतकमलोत्पला
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णा अप्सरोगणसेविता

viśālā nalinī yatra prabhūtakamalotpalā
haṁsakāraṇḍavākīrṇā apsarogaṇasevitā

There (you will behold) the charming mansion of Kuvera, resembling pale clouds, of burnished gold, built by Visvakarma; where (lies) the spacious tank overflowing with lotuses and lilies, thronged with swans and Karandavas, and frequented by troops of Apsaras.

तत्र वैश्रवणो राजा सर्वभूतनमस्कृतः
धनदो रमते श्रीमान्गुह्यकैः सह यक्षराट्

tatra vaiśravaṇo rājā sarvabhūtanamaskṛtaḥ
dhanado ramate śrīmānguhyakaiḥ saha yakṣarāṭ
There king Vaisravana, the lord of Yaksas, bowed down to by all creatures,-the graceful giver of riches—sporteth along with the Guhyakas.

तस्य चन्द्रनिकशेषु पर्वतेषु गुहासु च
रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः

tasya candranikaśeṣu parvateṣu guhāsu ca
rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyastatastataḥ
In the offshoots belonging to Kailasa resembling the moon, as also in their caverns, do you thoroughly search for Ravana in company with Vaidehi.

क्रौञ्चं तु गिरिमासाद्य बिलं तस्य सुदुर्गमम्
अप्रमत्तैः प्रवेष्टव्यं दुष्प्रवेशं हि तत्स्मृतम्

krauñcaṁ tu girimāsādya bilaṁ tasya sudurgamam
apramattaiḥ praveṣṭavyaṁ duṣpraveśaṁ hi tatsmṛtam
And coming to the Kruncha mountain, you should, having your wits about you, enter its inaccessible cavern; for that is well known as difficult of entrance.

वसन्ति हि महात्मानस्तत्र सूर्यसमप्रभाः
देवैरप्यर्चिताः सम्यग्देवरूपा महर्षयः

vasanti hi mahātmānastatra sūryasamaprabhāḥ
devairapyarcitāḥ samyagdevarūpā maharṣayaḥ
There dwell certain Maharsis, high-souled, of effulgence resembling that of the sun-complete god-like shapes,—who are sought by the deities themselves.

क्रौञ्चस्य तु गुहाश्चान्याः सानूनि शिखराणि च
निर्दराश्च नितम्बाश्च विचेतव्यास्ततस्ततः

krauñcasya tu guhāścānyāḥ sānūni śikharāṇi ca
nirdarāśca nitambāśca vicetavyāstatastataḥ
And you should thoroughly explore the other caves of Krauncha, its plateaus and peaks; its passes and sides.

क्रौञ्चस्य शिखरं चापि निरीक्ष्य च ततस्ततः
अवृक्षं कामशैलं च मानसं विहगालयम्

krauñcasya śikharaṁ cāpi nirīkṣya ca tatastataḥ
avṛkṣaṁ kāmaśailaṁ ca mānasaṁ vihagālayam
(Then is) the treeless Manasa-abode of birds-the scene of Kama's austerities. Way there is none for creatures, or for gods, or for Raksasas.

क्रौञ्चं गिरिमतिक्रम्य मैनाको नाम पर्वतः
मयस्य भवनं तत्र दानवस्य स्वयं कृतम्

krauñcaṁ girimatikramya maināko nāma parvataḥ
mayasya bhavanaṁ tatra dānavasya svayaṁ kṛtam
are That also must be explored by you, that mountain with plains and plateous. Going beyond Krauncha, (you shall see) the mountain, named Mainaka.

मैनाकस्तु विचेतव्यः ससानुप्रस्थकन्दरः
स्त्रीणामश्वमुखीनां च निकेतास्तत्र तत्र तु

mainākastu vicetavyaḥ sasānuprasthakandaraḥ
strīṇāmaśvamukhīnāṁ ca niketāstatra tatra tu
There is the residence of the Danvava, Maya, reared by himself. Mainaka also with its plains, plateaus and woods must be searched by you.

वन्द्यास्ते तु तपःसिद्धास्तापसा वीतकल्मषाः
प्रष्टव्याश्चापि सीतायाः प्रवृत्तं विनयान्वितैः

vandyāste tu tapaḥsiddhāstāpasā vītakalmaṣāḥ
praṣṭavyāścāpi sītāyāḥ pravṛttaṁ vinayānvitaiḥ

There are all over, the homes of females with faces resembling those of horses. Going beyond that part, (you shall come to) the asylum inhabited by Siddhas; where ascetics—Valakhilyas, Siddhas and Vaikhanasas. Saluting those Siddhas, who have been cleansed of their sins on account of their asceticism, you should in humble guise ask them concerning Sita.

हेमपुष्करसंछन्नं तत्र वैखानसं सरः
तरुणादित्यसंकाशैर्हंसैर्विचरितं शुभैः

hemapuṣkarasaṁchannaṁ tatra vaikhānasaṁ saraḥ
taruṇādityasaṁkāśairhaṁsairvicaritaṁ śubhaiḥ
There is the Vaikhanasa tank filled with golden lotuses; and ranged by graceful cranes of the hue of the infant sun.

औपवाह्यः कुबेरस्य सर्वभौम इति स्मृतः
गजः पर्येति तं देशं सदा सह करेणुभिः

aupavāhyaḥ kuberasya sarvabhauma iti smṛtaḥ
gajaḥ paryeti taṁ deśaṁ sadā saha kareṇubhiḥ
Kuvera's vehicle, the elephant known (by the name of) Sarvabhauma, ever rangeth that country in company with she-elephants.

गभस्तिभिरिवार्कस्य स तु देशः प्रकाशते
विश्राम्यद्भिस्तपः सिद्धैर्देवकल्पैः स्वयम्प्रभैः

gabhastibhirivārkasya sa tu deśaḥ prakāśate
viśrāmyadbhistapaḥ siddhairdevakalpaiḥ svayamprabhaiḥ

Going beyond that expanse of water, (you come upon) a sky void of stars, and where the sun and the moon have been put out; and that land is visible by the rays, as if of the sun, proceeding from (the persons of) self-luminous, god-like ones, who are reposing there, after achieving success in austerities.

तं तु देशमतिक्रम्य शैलोदा नाम निम्नगा
उभयोस्तीरयोर्यस्याः कीचका नाम वेणवः

taṁ tu deśamatikramya śailodā nāma nimnagā
ubhayostīrayoryasyāḥ kīcakā nāma veṇavaḥ
Leaving behind that region, (you come to) a stream named Sailoda. On its both banks are bamboos named Kicaka.

ते नयन्ति परं तीरं सिद्धान्प्रत्यानयन्ति च
उत्तराः कुरवस्तत्र कृतपुण्यप्रतिश्रियाः

te nayanti paraṁ tīraṁ siddhānpratyānayanti ca
uttarāḥ kuravastatra kṛtapuṇyapratiśriyāḥ
These take the Siddhas to the other shore and bring them back again. There (are seen the northern Kurus, the abode of those that have acquired religious merit.

ततः काञ्चनपद्माभिः पद्मिनीभिः कृतोदकाः
नीलवैदूर्यपत्राढ्या नद्यस्तत्र सहस्रशः

tataḥ kāñcanapadmābhiḥ padminībhiḥ kṛtodakāḥ
nīlavaidūryapatrāḍhyā nadyastatra sahasraśaḥ
And there are tanks there with their waters crowned with golden lotuses. There are rivers by thousands with copious blue lapis leaves.

रक्तोत्पलवनैश्चात्र मण्डिताश्च हिरण्मयैः
तरुणादित्यसदृशैर्भान्ति तत्र जलाशयाः

raktotpalavanaiścātra maṇḍitāśca hiraṇmayaiḥ
taruṇādityasadṛśairbhānti tatra jalāśayāḥ
And the pools here, resembling the tender sun, are embellished with assemblages of golden red lotuses.

महार्हमणिपत्रैश्च काञ्चनप्रभ केसरैः
नीलोत्पलवनैश्चित्रैः स देशः सर्वतोवृतः

mahārhamaṇipatraiśca kāñcanaprabha kesaraiḥ
nīlotpalavanaiścitraiḥ sa deśaḥ sarvatovṛtaḥ
And that tract is every where filled with costly gems, and jewels, and woods of blue lotuses, having filaments splendid like gold; and with round pearls and costly jewels.

निस्तुलाभिश्च मुक्ताभिर्मणिभिश्च महाधनैः
उद्भूतपुलिनास्तत्र जातरूपैश्च निम्नगाः

nistulābhiśca muktābhirmaṇibhiśca mahādhanaiḥ
udbhūtapulināstatra jātarūpaiśca nimnagāḥ
And the rivers there have islets covered with gold; and are crowded with lovely hills of gold, bright as fire, furnished with all kinds of precious stones.

नित्यपुष्पफलाश्चात्र नगाः पत्ररथाकुलाः
दिव्यगन्धरसस्पर्शाः सर्वकामान्स्रवन्ति च

nityapuṣpaphalāścātra nagāḥ patrarathākulāḥ
divyagandharasasparśāḥ sarvakāmānsravanti ca
And the trees there, thronged with birds, bear flowers and fruits daily; and, charged with savoury juices, publishing superb perfumes, and of delicious feel, they confer every wish.

नानाकाराणि वासांसि फलन्त्यन्ये नगोत्तमाः
मुक्तावैदूर्यचित्राणि भूषणानि तथैव च

nānākārāṇi vāsāṁsi phalantyanye nagottamāḥ
muktāvaidūryacitrāṇi bhūṣaṇāni tathaiva ca

Other excellent trees bring forth attires of divers kinds, and ornaments decked with pearls and lapises,-coveted alike by males and females*. *The present text, according to Kataka, drops a sloka, whose last line is, Beings possessed of powerful effulgence, sport here always in company with females.

स्त्रीणां यान्यनुरूपाणि पुरुषाणां तथैव च
सर्वर्तुसुखसेव्यानि फलन्त्यन्ये नगोत्तमाः

strīṇāṁ yānyanurūpāṇi puruṣāṇāṁ tathaiva ca
sarvartusukhasevyāni phalantyanye nagottamāḥ
And other excellent trees bear fruits fit to be partaken at all seasons. And other excellent trees bring forth precious beds dight with costly jewels and furnished with variegated covers.

स्त्रियश्च गुणसंपन्ना रूपयौवनलक्षिताः
गन्धर्वाः किंनरा सिद्धा नागा विद्याधरास्तथा
रमन्ते सहितास्तत्र नारीभिर्भास्करप्रभाः

striyaśca guṇasaṁpannā rūpayauvanalakṣitāḥ
gandharvāḥ kiṁnarā siddhā nāgā vidyādharāstathā
ramante sahitāstatra nārībhirbhāskaraprabhāḥ

And other trees bring forth charming wreaths, and costly drinks, and various kinds of viands. And females adorned with every accomplishment, and endowed with youth and beauty, and Gandharvas and Kinnaras, and Siddhas and Nagas and Vidyadharas, of blazing splendour, ceaselessly sport there in company with females.

सर्वे सुकृतकर्माणः सर्वे रतिपरायणाः
सर्वे कामार्थसहिता वसन्ति सह योषितः

sarve sukṛtakarmāṇaḥ sarve ratiparāyaṇāḥ
sarve kāmārthasahitā vasanti saha yoṣitaḥ
And all of righteous deeds, and all engaged in amorous disports, and all furnished with desire and profit,-dwell in that place in association with their females.

गीतवादित्रनिर्घोषः सोत्कृष्टहसितस्वनः
श्रूयते सततं तत्र सर्वभूतमनोहरः

gītavāditranirghoṣaḥ sotkṛṣṭahasitasvanaḥ
śrūyate satataṁ tatra sarvabhūtamanoharaḥ
And there are continually heard there the sounds of instruments and the voice of song mixed with sweet hilarious laughter, capable of taking all crcatures.

तत्र नामुदितः कश्चिन्नास्ति कश्चिदसत्प्रियः
अहन्यहनि वर्धन्ते गुणास्तत्र मनोरमाः

tatra nāmuditaḥ kaścinnāsti kaścidasatpriyaḥ
ahanyahani vardhante guṇāstatra manoramāḥ
No one is depressed there; nor does any one there want any desirable object; and day after day the delightful qualities find their development there.

समतिक्रम्य तं देशमुत्तरस्तोयसां निधिः
तत्र सोमगिरिर्नाम मध्ये हेममयो महान्

samatikramya taṁ deśamuttarastoyasāṁ nidhiḥ
tatra somagirirnāma madhye hemamayo mahān
Passing beyond that is the Northern ocean. In the bosom (of the deep) is the mountain named Somagiri, golden and of great dimensions.

स तु देशो विसूर्योऽपि तस्य भासा प्रकाशते
सूर्यलक्ष्म्याभिविज्ञेयस्तपसेव विवस्वता

sa tu deśo visūryo'pi tasya bhāsā prakāśate
sūryalakṣmyābhivijñeyastapaseva vivasvatā
Albeit without the sun, yet through the brightness of the Soma mountain, the land shines forth with all the loveliness and reality of one warmed by the sun.

भगवानपि विश्वात्मा शम्भुरेकादशात्मकः
ब्रह्मा वसति देवेशो ब्रह्मर्षिपरिवारितः

bhagavānapi viśvātmā śambhurekādaśātmakaḥ
brahmā vasati deveśo brahmarṣiparivāritaḥ
There that Soul of the Universe, the adorable Sambhu, fraught with the spirits of the eleven Rudras-that lord of the gods-Brahma.dwelleth, surrounded by the Brahmarsis.

न कथंचन गन्तव्यं कुरूणामुत्तरेण वः
अन्येषामपि भूतानां नातिक्रामति वै गतिः

na kathaṁcana gantavyaṁ kurūṇāmuttareṇa vaḥ
anyeṣāmapi bhūtānāṁ nātikrāmati vai gatiḥ
You cannot proceed to the north of the Kurus; nor is there way in that region for any other creatures.

सा हि सोमगिरिर्नाम देवानामपि दुर्गमः
तमालोक्य ततः क्षिप्रमुपावर्तितुमर्हथ

sā hi somagirirnāma devānāmapi durgamaḥ
tamālokya tataḥ kṣipramupāvartitumarhatha
And that mountain is named Soma, incapable of being entered even by the gods, Sighting this you should speedily turn back.

एतावद्वानरैः शक्यं गन्तुं वानरपुंगवाः
अभास्करममर्यादं न जानीमस्ततः परम्

etāvadvānaraiḥ śakyaṁ gantuṁ vānarapuṁgavāḥ
abhāskaramamaryādaṁ na jānīmastataḥ param
You foremost of monkey, the monkeys are competent to proceed thus far. Beyond that, of regions sunless and limitless I know nothing.

सर्वमेतद्विचेतव्यं यन्मया परिकीर्तितम्
यदन्यदपि नोक्तं च तत्रापि क्रियतां मतिः

sarvametadvicetavyaṁ yanmayā parikīrtitam
yadanyadapi noktaṁ ca tatrāpi kriyatāṁ matiḥ
You should search all these which I have described (to you); and you should also turn your attention to others besides, which I have omitted to mention.

ततः कृतं दाशरथेर्महत्प्रियं; महत्तरं चापि ततो मम प्रियम्
कृतं भविष्यत्यनिलानलोपमा; विदेहजा दर्शनजेन कर्मणा

tataḥ kṛtaṁ dāśarathermahatpriyaṁ; mahattaraṁ cāpi tato mama priyam
kṛtaṁ bhaviṣyatyanilānalopamā; videhajā darśanajena karmaṇā

You that are comparable to the wind or fire, by accomplishing the work of beholding Videha's daughter, you will do what is held as exceedingly dear to Dasaratha's son as well as highly grateful to me.

ततः कृतार्थाः सहिताः सबान्धवा; मयार्चिताः सर्वगुणैर्मनोरमैः
चरिष्यथोर्वीं प्रतिशान्तशत्रवः; सहप्रिया भूतधराः प्लवंगमाः

tataḥ kṛtārthāḥ sahitāḥ sabāndhavā; mayārcitāḥ sarvaguṇairmanoramaiḥ
cariṣyathorvīṁ pratiśāntaśatravaḥ; sahapriyā bhūtadharāḥ plavaṁgamāḥ

Then, having achieved success, do you, along with your friends, honoured by me, and crowned with every virtue, you monkeys, with your enemies slain, range the earth in company with your wives,-the support of all beings.

विशेषेण तु सुग्रीवो हनुमत्यर्थमुक्तवान्
स हि तस्मिन्हरिश्रेष्ठे निश्चितार्थोऽर्थसाधने

viśeṣeṇa tu sugrīvo hanumatyarthamuktavān
sa hi tasminhariśreṣṭhe niścitārtho'rthasādhane
Sugriva had declared his conviction that he relied particularly upon Hanuman.

न भूमौ नान्तरिक्षे वा नाम्बरे नामरालये
नाप्सु वा गतिसंगं ते पश्यामि हरिपुंगव

na bhūmau nāntarikṣe vā nāmbare nāmarālaye
nāpsu vā gatisaṁgaṁ te paśyāmi haripuṁgava

O foremost of monkeys, neither on the earth, nor in the sky', nor in the etherial regions, nor yet in water, find I any obstacle to your course. 1. Antariksa-regions above the earth in which the birds fly. 2. Ambara— Upper air.

सासुराः सहगन्धर्वाः सनागनरदेवताः
विदिताः सर्वलोकास्ते ससागरधराधराः

sāsurāḥ sahagandharvāḥ sanāganaradevatāḥ
viditāḥ sarvalokāste sasāgaradharādharāḥ
The entire worlds with Asuras, and Gandharvas, and Nagas, and men, and gods, with oceans, and the earth and the regions beneath—are well known to you.

गतिर्वेगश्च तेजश्च लाघवं च महाकपे
पितुस्ते सदृशं वीर मारुतस्य महौजसः

gatirvegaśca tejaśca lāghavaṁ ca mahākape
pituste sadṛśaṁ vīra mārutasya mahaujasaḥ

And your motion, vehemence, energy and fleetness, are, O hero, O mighty ape, even like those of your sire, the powerful wind god; and there exists no creature on earth that is like to you in energy. Therefore do you bethink you how Sita may be recovered.

त्वय्येव हनुमन्नस्ति बलं बुद्धिः पराक्रमः
देशकालानुवृत्तश्च नयश्च नयपण्डित

tvayyeva hanumannasti balaṁ buddhiḥ parākramaḥ
deśakālānuvṛttaśca nayaśca nayapaṇḍita
Even in you, O you versed in policy, are strength, and wit, and courage, and policy, and conduct in consonance with season and place.

ततः कार्यसमासंगमवगम्य हनूमति
विदित्वा हनुमन्तं च चिन्तयामास राघवः

tataḥ kāryasamāsaṁgamavagamya hanūmati
viditvā hanumantaṁ ca cintayāmāsa rāghavaḥ
Thereat, understanding that success in the task depended upon Hanuman, and also knowing what Hanuman was, Raghava reflected,

सर्वथा निश्चितार्थोऽयं हनूमति हरीश्वरः
निश्चितार्थतरश्चापि हनूमान्कार्यसाधने

sarvathā niścitārtho'yaṁ hanūmati harīśvaraḥ
niścitārthataraścāpi hanūmānkāryasādhane
This lord of monkeys is every way confident concerning Hanuman; and Hanuman himself is even more confident of achieving success in the work.

तदेवं प्रस्थितस्यास्य परिज्ञातस्य कर्मभिः
भर्त्रा परिगृहीतस्य ध्रुवः कार्यफलोदयः

tadevaṁ prasthitasyāsya parijñātasya karmabhiḥ
bhartrā parigṛhītasya dhruvaḥ kāryaphalodayaḥ
He that has been tested by his deed, and who has been considered worthiest by his master, having veen commissioned in this business,-success in the work is certain.

तं समीक्ष्य महातेजा व्यवसायोत्तरं हरिम्
कृतार्थ इव संवृत्तः प्रहृष्टेन्द्रियमानसः

taṁ samīkṣya mahātejā vyavasāyottaraṁ harim
kṛtārtha iva saṁvṛttaḥ prahṛṣṭendriyamānasaḥ

Then beholding that monkey who was the fittest for the task, that exceedingly energetic senses one, (Rama), with his mind and exhilarated, considering himself as already crowned with success, felt the excess of joy.

ददौ तस्य ततः प्रीतः स्वनामाङ्कोपशोभितम्
अङ्गुलीयमभिज्ञानं राजपुत्र्याः परंतपः

dadau tasya tataḥ prītaḥ svanāmāṅkopaśobhitam
aṅgulīyamabhijñānaṁ rājaputryāḥ paraṁtapaḥ
And well pleased, that subduer of enemies handed to Hanuman a ring inscribed with his name, as a sign to the king's daughter.

अनेन त्वां हरिश्रेष्ठ चिह्नेन जनकात्मजा
मत्सकाशादनुप्राप्तमनुद्विग्नानुपश्यति

anena tvāṁ hariśreṣṭha cihnena janakātmajā
matsakāśādanuprāptamanudvignānupaśyati
By this sign, O foremost of monkeys, Janaka's daughter will be able to see you fearlessly, as one that has come from me.

व्यवसायश्च ते वीर सत्त्वयुक्तश्च विक्रमः
सुग्रीवस्य च संदेशः सिद्धिं कथयतीव मे

vyavasāyaśca te vīra sattvayuktaśca vikramaḥ
sugrīvasya ca saṁdeśaḥ siddhiṁ kathayatīva me
Your firmness, O hero, and sterling prowess, as well as Sugriva's saying, tell me greatly of success.

स तद्गृह्य हरिश्रेष्ठः स्थाप्य मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः
वन्दित्वा चरणौ चैव प्रस्थितः प्लवगोत्तमः

sa tadgṛhya hariśreṣṭhaḥ sthāpya mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ
vanditvā caraṇau caiva prasthitaḥ plavagottamaḥ
Thereupon, taking that (ring), and raising his joined palms to his head, that foremost and best of monkeys, saluting (Rama's) feet, went away.

स तत्प्रकर्षन्हरिणां बलं मह;द्बभूव वीरः पवनात्मजः कपि
गताम्बुदे व्योम्नि विशुद्धमण्डलः; शशीव नक्षत्रगणोपशोभितः

sa tatprakarṣanhariṇāṁ balaṁ maha;dbabhūva vīraḥ pavanātmajaḥ kapi
gatāmbude vyomni viśuddhamaṇḍalaḥ; śaśīva nakṣatragaṇopaśobhitaḥ
Then taking with him that mighty host of monkeys, that hero, the son of the wind, resembled the moon of bright disc in the sky, garnished by the stars, after the clouds have departed.

अतिबलबलमाश्रितस्तवाहं; हरिवरविक्रमविक्रमैरनल्पैः
पवनसुत यथाभिगम्यते सा; जनकसुता हनुमंस्तथा कुरुष्व

atibalabalamāśritastavāhaṁ; harivaravikramavikramairanalpaiḥ
pavanasuta yathābhigamyate sā; janakasutā hanumaṁstathā kuruṣva

O you of excessive strength! I take refuge in your mighty. O you endowed with the prowess of the foremost of lions! do you, O son of the Wind, O Hanuman, exert yourself so, summoning the great strength you are master of, that we may obtain Janaka's daughter.* The commentator says that this speech is equally attributable to Rama and Sugriva. But I think, it would fit Rama's lips to a nicely. The commentator says that this speech is equally attributable to Rama and Sugriva. But I think, it would fit Rama's lips to a nicely.

तदुग्रशासनं भर्तुर्विज्ञाय हरिपुंगवाः
शलभा इव संछाद्य मेदिनीं संप्रतस्थिरे

tadugraśāsanaṁ bharturvijñāya haripuṁgavāḥ
śalabhā iva saṁchādya medinīṁ saṁpratasthire
The monkey-chiefs, knowing the stern command of their lord should search in all these places. Then, covering up the earth like locusts, they marched away.

रामः प्रस्रवणे तस्मिन्न्यवसत्सहलक्ष्मणः
प्रतीक्षमाणस्तं मासं यः सीताधिगमे कृतः

rāmaḥ prasravaṇe tasminnyavasatsahalakṣmaṇaḥ
pratīkṣamāṇastaṁ māsaṁ yaḥ sītādhigame kṛtaḥ
Expecting tidings of Sita, Rama remained that month in the vicinity of that cascade, in company with Laksmana.

उत्तरां तु दिशं रम्यां गिरिराजसमावृताम्
प्रतस्थे सहसा वीरो हरिः शतबलिस्तदा

uttarāṁ tu diśaṁ ramyāṁ girirājasamāvṛtām
pratasthe sahasā vīro hariḥ śatabalistadā
And that heroic monkey Satavali swiftly set out for the northern regions covered by the monarch of mountains.

पश्चिमां तु दिशं घोरां सुषेणः प्लवगेश्वरः
प्रतस्थे हरिशार्दूलो भृशं वरुणपालिताम्

paścimāṁ tu diśaṁ ghorāṁ suṣeṇaḥ plavageśvaraḥ
pratasthe hariśārdūlo bhṛśaṁ varuṇapālitām

And that leader of monkey herds, Vinata, proceeded towards the estern quarter. And that monkey, Hanuman-leader of monkeyherds in company with Tara, Angada and others, went to the South, inhabited by Agastya. And that lord of monkeys, Susena, lion among monkeys, went to the terrible western quarter, protected by Varuna.

ततः सर्वा दिशो राजा चोदयित्वा यथा तथम्
कपिसेना पतीन्मुख्यान्मुमोद सुखितः सुखम्

tataḥ sarvā diśo rājā codayitvā yathā tatham
kapisenā patīnmukhyānmumoda sukhitaḥ sukham
Then, having properly despatched (his forces) in all directions, that general of the monkey hosts, being pleased, gave himself up to sport.

एवं संचोदिताः सर्वे राज्ञा वानरयूथपाः
स्वां स्वां दिशमभिप्रेत्य त्वरिताः संप्रतस्थिरे

evaṁ saṁcoditāḥ sarve rājñā vānarayūthapāḥ
svāṁ svāṁ diśamabhipretya tvaritāḥ saṁpratasthire
Thus despatched by the king, the monkeychiefs proceeded apace respectively towards their destined quarters.

इत्येकैकं तदा तत्र वानरा बलदर्पिताः
ऊचुश्च वचनं तस्मिन्हरिराजस्य संनिधौ

ityekaikaṁ tadā tatra vānarā baladarpitāḥ
ūcuśca vacanaṁ tasminharirājasya saṁnidhau
Thus did the apes proud of their strength, severally speak in presence of the sovereign of the monkeys.

गतेषु वानरेन्द्रेषु रामः सुग्रीवमब्रवीत्
कथं भवान्विनाजीते सर्वं वै मण्डलं भुवः

gateṣu vānarendreṣu rāmaḥ sugrīvamabravīt
kathaṁ bhavānvinājīte sarvaṁ vai maṇḍalaṁ bhuvaḥ
On the monkey-chiefs having departed, Rama said to Sugriva, How is it that you know all the quarters of this earth?'

सुग्रीवस्तु ततो राममुवाच प्रणतात्मवान्
श्रूयतां सर्वमाख्यास्ये विस्तरेण नरर्षभ

sugrīvastu tato rāmamuvāca praṇatātmavān
śrūyatāṁ sarvamākhyāsye vistareṇa nararṣabha
Thereupon, the self-controlled Sugriva, bowing low, said to Rama, Do you listen to my words. I shall relate everything.

तदा विवेश महिषो मलयस्य गुहां प्रति
विवेश वाली तत्रापि मलयं तज्जिघांसया

tadā viveśa mahiṣo malayasya guhāṁ prati
viveśa vālī tatrāpi malayaṁ tajjighāṁsayā
When Vali pursued the Danava Dundubhi, wearing the form of a buffalo towards the Malaya mountain, Mahisa entered a cave of that mountain. And Vali also, desirous of slaying the Asura, entered Malaya.

ततोऽहं तत्र निक्षिप्तो गुहाद्वारिविनीतवत्
न च निष्क्रमते वाली तदा संवत्सरे गते

tato'haṁ tatra nikṣipto guhādvārivinītavat
na ca niṣkramate vālī tadā saṁvatsare gate
And I was made to stand at the mouth in humble guise; nor did Vali issue out, although a good year rolled away.

ततः क्षतजवेगेन आपुपूरे तदा बिलम्
तदहं विस्मितो दृष्ट्वा भ्रातृशोकविषार्दितः

tataḥ kṣatajavegena āpupūre tadā bilam
tadahaṁ vismito dṛṣṭvā bhrātṛśokaviṣārditaḥ
Then the cave became filled with blood gushing out vehemently. Seeing this, I became amazed, and exercised with the poison of grief of accountri my brother.

अथाहं कृतबुद्धिस्तु सुव्यक्तं निहतो गुरुः
शिलापर्वतसंकाशा बिलद्वारि मया कृता
अशक्नुवन्निष्क्रमितुं महिषो विनशेदिति

athāhaṁ kṛtabuddhistu suvyaktaṁ nihato guruḥ
śilāparvatasaṁkāśā biladvāri mayā kṛtā
aśaknuvanniṣkramituṁ mahiṣo vinaśediti
And I, losing my sense, thought that my superior had for certain been slain. And I placed 7 crag huge as a hill at the mouth of the cave. took to my

ततोऽहमागां किष्किन्धां निराशस्तस्य जीविते
राज्यं च सुमहत्प्राप्तं तारा च रुमया सह
मित्रैश्च सहितस्तत्र वसामि विगतज्वरः

tato'hamāgāṁ kiṣkindhāṁ nirāśastasya jīvite
rājyaṁ ca sumahatprāptaṁ tārā ca rumayā saha
mitraiśca sahitastatra vasāmi vigatajvaraḥ
And obtaining the spacious kingdom along with Tara and Uma, I began to pass my days in peace in company with his counsellors.

स मां जिघांसुर्दुष्टात्मा वाली प्रव्यथितेन्द्रियः
परिलाकयते क्रोधाद्धावन्तं सचिवैः सह

sa māṁ jighāṁsurduṣṭātmā vālī pravyathitendriyaḥ
parilākayate krodhāddhāvantaṁ sacivaiḥ saha

Then came that foremost of monkeys, having slain him (Mahisa). Thereupon I, influenced by fear, in consideration of his dignity, made over to him his monarchy. But Vali, his senses exercised with sorrow, anxious to slay me, in company with his counsellors, pursued me, who heels.

ततोऽहं वालिना तेन सानुबन्धः प्रधावितः
नदीश्च विविधाः पश्यन्वनानि नगराणि च

tato'haṁ vālinā tena sānubandhaḥ pradhāvitaḥ
nadīśca vividhāḥ paśyanvanāni nagarāṇi ca

Hotly pursued and chased by Vali, I surveyed various streams and woods and cities. And I surveyed the earth like the hoof-print of a cow, or the image reflected from a mirror, or a firebrand whirled (in the air).* *The commentator remarks that like the hoof-print of a cow expresses the case with which Sugriva travelled the earth; like a fire brand whirled conveys his vehement speed; and like the image reflected on a mirror signifies the lucidity of his perception.

इदानीं मे स्मृतं राजन्यथा वाली हरीश्वरः
मतङ्गेन तदा शप्तो ह्यस्मिन्नाश्रममण्डले

idānīṁ me smṛtaṁ rājanyathā vālī harīśvaraḥ
mataṅgena tadā śapto hyasminnāśramamaṇḍale
'O king, now, I remember me how that lord of monkeys, Vali, was cursed by Matanga in this very hermitage. If Vali enters (into this asylum), his head becomes cleft in hundred.

ततः पर्वतमासाद्य ऋश्यमूकं नृपात्मज
न विवेश तदा वाली मतङ्गस्य भयात्तदा

tataḥ parvatamāsādya ṛśyamūkaṁ nṛpātmaja
na viveśa tadā vālī mataṅgasya bhayāttadā
There shall dwell happily without anxiety.' O king's son, thereupon, we went to the Risyamuka mountain, nor did then Vali enter we there from fear of Matanga.

एवं मया तदा राजन्प्रत्यक्षमुपलक्षितम्
पृथिवीमण्डलं कृत्स्नं गुहामस्म्यागतस्ततः

evaṁ mayā tadā rājanpratyakṣamupalakṣitam
pṛthivīmaṇḍalaṁ kṛtsnaṁ guhāmasmyāgatastataḥ
Thus, O king, did I actually see all the world. And from that place I came to this cave.

दर्शनार्थं तु वैदेह्याः सर्वतः कपियूथपाः
व्यादिष्टाः कपिराजेन यथोक्तं जग्मुरञ्जसा

darśanārthaṁ tu vaidehyāḥ sarvataḥ kapiyūthapāḥ
vyādiṣṭāḥ kapirājena yathoktaṁ jagmurañjasā
The principal monkeys, having been ordered by the monkey-king, speedily went in all directions to their destinations for the purpose of seeing Vaidehi.

सरांसि सरितः कक्षानाकाशं नगराणि च
नदीदुर्गांस्तथा शैलान्विचिन्वन्ति समन्ततः

sarāṁsi saritaḥ kakṣānākāśaṁ nagarāṇi ca
nadīdurgāṁstathā śailānvicinvanti samantataḥ
And on all sides they explore watery expanses, and streams, and lawns, and commons, and cities, and tracts rendered impassable by torrents.

सुग्रीवेण समाख्यातान्सर्वे वानरयूथपाः
प्रदेशान्प्रविचिन्वन्ति सशैलवनकाननान्

sugrīveṇa samākhyātānsarve vānarayūthapāḥ
pradeśānpravicinvanti saśailavanakānanān
And the leaders of monkey-herds search all those countries, countries, described described by Sugriva,-containing mountains, woods and forests.

विचिन्त्य दिवसं सर्वे सीताधिगमने धृताः
समायान्ति स्म मेदिन्यां निशाकालेशु वानराः

vicintya divasaṁ sarve sītādhigamane dhṛtāḥ
samāyānti sma medinyāṁ niśākāleśu vānarāḥ
Engaged during the day in search of Sita, at night the monkeys seek the ground (for sleep).

सर्वर्तुकांश्च देशेषु वानराः सफलान्द्रुमान्
आसाद्य रजनीं शय्यां चक्रुः सर्वेष्वहःसु ते

sarvartukāṁśca deśeṣu vānarāḥ saphalāndrumān
āsādya rajanīṁ śayyāṁ cakruḥ sarveṣvahaḥsu te

In every place, by day coming to trees aye enjoying every season, and crowned with fruits, the monkeys prepared their beds at night.* *The sense is rather obscure, it being difficult to understand the relation their beds bore to the neighbouring trees.

तदहः प्रथमं कृत्वा मासे प्रस्रवणं गताः
कपिराजेन संगम्य निराशाः कपियूथपाः

tadahaḥ prathamaṁ kṛtvā māse prasravaṇaṁ gatāḥ
kapirājena saṁgamya nirāśāḥ kapiyūthapāḥ
Counting that day* as the first, the principal monkeys, after the month had run out, resigning all hope, came to the Fountain and met with the monkey-king. *i.e. the day of their departure.

विचित्य तु दिशं पूर्वां यथोक्तां सचिवैः सह
अदृष्ट्वा विनतः सीतामाजगाम महाबलः

vicitya tu diśaṁ pūrvāṁ yathoktāṁ sacivaiḥ saha
adṛṣṭvā vinataḥ sītāmājagāma mahābalaḥ
And having explored the Eastern regions, as directed, the exceedingly strong Vinata not having been able to see Sita, came back, in company with his counsellors.

उत्तरां तु दिशं सर्वां विचित्य स महाकपिः
आगतः सह सैन्येन वीरः शतबलिस्तदा

uttarāṁ tu diśaṁ sarvāṁ vicitya sa mahākapiḥ
āgataḥ saha sainyena vīraḥ śatabalistadā
And then that mighty ape, Satavali, daunted in spirits, arrived with his forces, after having searched all through the North.

सुषेणः पश्चिमामाशां विचित्य सह वानरैः
समेत्य मासे संपूर्णे सुग्रीवमुपचक्रमे

suṣeṇaḥ paścimāmāśāṁ vicitya saha vānaraiḥ
sametya māse saṁpūrṇe sugrīvamupacakrame
And having searched the West in company with his monkeys, Susena, on the month being complete, presented himself before Sugriva.

तं प्रस्रवणपृष्ठस्थं समासाद्याभिवाद्य च
आसीनं सह रामेण सुग्रीवमिदमब्रुवन्

taṁ prasravaṇapṛṣṭhasthaṁ samāsādyābhivādya ca
āsīnaṁ saha rāmeṇa sugrīvamidamabruvan
And coming to Sugriva seated along with Rama behind the Fountain, and saluting the former, Susena said to Sugriva.

गहनेषु च देशेषु दुर्गेषु विषमेषु च
सत्त्वान्यतिप्रमाणानि विचितानि हतानि च
ये चैव गहना देशा विचितास्ते पुनः पुनः

gahaneṣu ca deśeṣu durgeṣu viṣameṣu ca
sattvānyatipramāṇāni vicitāni hatāni ca
ye caiva gahanā deśā vicitāste punaḥ punaḥ

Searched have been all the mountains, and deep woods, and streams, and islands embosomed in the ocean, and the various provinces. And also searched have been all the caves which have been described by you; and searched have been all the groves entertwined with plants; and thickets; and difficult and uneven grounds. And huge animals have been sought out and slain (by us). And all the impracticable places we have explored again and again.

उदारसत्त्वाभिजनो महात्मा; स मैथिलीं द्रक्ष्यति वानरेन्द्रः
दिशं तु यामेव गता तु सीता; तामास्थितो वायुसुतो हनूमान्

udārasattvābhijano mahātmā; sa maithilīṁ drakṣyati vānarendraḥ
diśaṁ tu yāmeva gatā tu sītā; tāmāsthito vāyusuto hanūmān
